# Xiaomi Pad 7 / 7 Pro Keyboard Fix

Hardware keyboard fixes for the **Xiaomi Pad 7 (`uke`)** and **Pad 7 Pro (`muyu`)** running custom AOSP or crDroid ROMs.

Restores typing at boot, fixes landscape arrow key rotation, enables the Caps Lock LED, adds keyboard backlight shortcuts, and resolves excessive CPU usage caused by Xiaomi&#x27;s touch telemetry service.

## Quick Install — Magisk / KernelSU

1. Download **Xiaomi-Pad7-Keyboard-Fix-All-in-One.zip** from the [latest release](https://github.com/saksham-991/xiaomi-keyboard-fix/releases/tag/Magisk-Module).
2. Install the ZIP through Magisk or KernelSU.
3. Reboot your tablet.

&gt;Magisk Module is **not needed** to install, it is just for convenience, manual steps to write out all the commands are given below which essentially do the exact same thing that this module does.

## Problems Solved

| Problem | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Keyboard connects but cannot type | `xiaomi_kbd_service.sh` automates HID rebinding at boot and when the keyboard connects. |
| Keyboard stops working after a few minutes | `kbd_auth.sh` and `tokenhelper` provide MiAuth tokens locally through TrustZone. |
| Arrow keys are rotated 90° in landscape | `kbd_idc.sh` generates the IDC configuration early in boot with `device.internal = 0`. |
| Caps Lock LED does not work | `kbd_leds.sh` watches input events and synchronizes the LED state. |
| Keyboard backlight cannot be adjusted | `kbd_leds.sh` adds configurable brightness shortcuts. |
| Tablet overheats or one CPU core stays at 100% | `kbd_no_toucheventcheck.sh` disables the broken MiSight touch telemetry loop. |

&gt; The 30hz touchpad issue (choppy pointer) is also solved in the magisk module as it is a simple toggle &quot;Disable HW Overlays&quot; IN developer options, I added it here because the touchpad is on the same keyboard folio case, otherwise its basically a ROM issue, rather than a Keyboard issue.

### Security and Privacy

No keystrokes are logged. Authentication keys are not extracted or sent online. Authentication tokens are computed locally using the stock firmware&#x27;s `devauth` trustlets.

## Manual Installation

Use this method to install the fix through `/data/adb` boot scripts without installing a Magisk module.

### Prerequisites

- A Xiaomi Pad 7 or Pad 7 Pro running a custom ROM with stock HyperOS vendor blobs.
- Root access through Magisk or KernelSU.
- ADB Setup.
- The following three proprietary HAL files extracted from the `odm.img` partition of a stock HyperOS Recovery ROM&#x27;s payload.bin using EROFS:

  ```text
  /odm/bin/midevauthd
  /odm/lib64/libmidevauth.so
  /odm/lib64/vendor.xiaomi.hardware.aidl.midevauth-V1-ndk_platform.so
  ```

- The `tokenhelper` binary from the [latest release](https://github.com/JohnnyFFM/xiaomi-keyboard-fix/releases/latest), or a manually built copy.
- The scripts from this repository&#x27;s `device/` directory.

Check that the required firmware and device interface are present:

```sh
adb shell su -c &#x27;ls /vendor/firmware_mnt/image/devauth.*; ls /dev/smcinvoke&#x27;
```

### 1. Stage the Files

Run this command on your computer from the repository directory, with the extracted HAL files and `tokenhelper` in the current directory:

```sh
adb push \
  midevauthd \
  libmidevauth.so \
  vendor.xiaomi.hardware.aidl.midevauth-V1-ndk_platform.so \
  tokenhelper \
  device/kbd_auth.sh \
  device/kbd_leds.sh \
  device/service.d-kbdauth.sh \
  device/xiaomi_kbd_service.sh \
  device/post-fs-data-kbd-idc.sh \
  device/kbd_no_toucheventcheck.sh \
  /data/local/tmp/
```

### 2. Install the Files and Set Permissions

```sh
adb shell su -c &#x27;
mkdir -p /data/adb/kbdauth /data/adb/service.d /data/adb/post-fs-data.d

cp \
  /data/local/tmp/midevauthd \
  /data/local/tmp/libmidevauth.so \
  /data/local/tmp/vendor.xiaomi.hardware.aidl.midevauth-V1-ndk_platform.so \
  /data/local/tmp/tokenhelper \
  /data/local/tmp/kbd_auth.sh \
  /data/local/tmp/kbd_leds.sh \
  /data/adb/kbdauth/

cp /data/local/tmp/service.d-kbdauth.sh \
  /data/adb/service.d/kbdauth.sh

cp /data/local/tmp/xiaomi_kbd_service.sh \
  /data/adb/service.d/xiaomi_kbd_service.sh

cp /data/local/tmp/post-fs-data-kbd-idc.sh \
  /data/adb/post-fs-data.d/kbd_idc.sh

</pre>

## What this repository is

The umbrella repository for the Fedora 44 port to Xiaomi Pad 7 and POCO Pad X1
(`uke`, SM7675). It holds user and developer documentation, the upstream pin and
sync tooling, and three submodule forks:

| Path | Repository | What changes there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `senemos-uke-kernel/` | [senemos-uke-kernel-mainline](https://github.com/linuxgamer/senemos-uke-kernel-mainline) | Kernel, device trees, kernel RPMs |
| `uke-fedora-builder/` | [uke-fedora-builder](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora-builder) | Image recipes, rootfs, packaging |
| `uke-linux-hardware-support/` | [uke-linux-hardware-support](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-linux-hardware-support) | Device packages, boot integration, firmware payload rules |

`private/`, `build/` and `artifacts/` are local and gitignored. Never link to
them from published documents.

## Read order for a new session

1. [README.md](README.md) — what the project is and what hardware works.
2. [docs/DEVELOPING.md](docs/DEVELOPING.md) — environment, checks, contribution flow.
3. [docs/STATE.md](docs/STATE.md) — facts as of the last handoff.
4. [docs/BACKLOG.md](docs/BACKLOG.md) — ordered work with status.
5. [docs/UPSTREAM.md](docs/UPSTREAM.md) — the vendored-fork sync model.
6. The `AGENTS.md` of the component you are about to touch.

## Start of a session

```sh
git status
git submodule status
tools/check-dev-env.sh --quick
```

Then read the top of the backlog, pick one item, and say what you are doing and
which files you expect to write. Verify every fact you rely on: a stale document
is a bug, not context.

Rules:

- One backlog item per session unless it is a small follow-up in the same
  component.
- Update the backlog status in the same commit as the work.
- Do not start unrelated work in the same commit. Small doc fixes that the
  current change makes wrong belong in that change.
- If you cannot verify a claim, write that you could not verify it. Never turn
  an assumption into a status row.

## Working with submodules

The submodules are pinned to the gitlinks recorded in the umbrella. A clean
clone checks out detached commits; that is expected.

```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora.git
git submodule update --init --recursive   # after pulling a gitlink change
```

Flow for a component change:

1. Work and commit on a named branch in the component repository.
2. Push it and open the pull request in that component repository.
3. Run the component checks there and, for anything device-facing, the matching
   image smoke test ([docs/RELEASE.md](docs/RELEASE.md)).
4. Only after the component change is accepted, the umbrella updates the
   gitlink in a separate pull request. Do not bundle component commits into the
   umbrella.

Never move a gitlink &quot;to pick up a fix&quot; without saying which component commit it
points to and what was tested. Never rewrite a published tag or release asset.

## Task loop and definition of done

1. Pick the top unblocked item from `docs/BACKLOG.md`, or record a new item
   before starting.
2. Confirm scope and write down the files you own. Re-read a file before editing
   it; if it changed meanwhile, rebase your edit on the current content.
3. Implement the smallest change that satisfies the item.
4. Run the checks that cover the change, not only a syntax check (see below).
5. Update `docs/STATE.md` and the backlog status.
6. Commit in English, push, and fix CI if the change broke it.

Done means: the relevant checks passed (or their absence is stated), evidence is
recorded, docs are updated, no secret or OEM blob is committed, and any submodule
pointer move is intentional and explained.

## Checks

Full setup, expected outputs and known failure modes are in
[docs/DEVELOPING.md](docs/DEVELOPING.md#checks). The short version:

| Command | Covers | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tools/check-dev-env.sh` | Clone shape, submodules, host tools | Use `--quick` for docs-only work |
| `tools/check-docs.sh` | Relative links in published docs | Run for every documentation change |
| `tools/check-forbidden-paths.sh` | Removed trees: `referances/`, `reports/`, hardware top-level `docs/` | Run before a commit and after every sync |
| `make -C senemos-uke-kernel check-pins` | Source and manifest digests | Fast |
| `make -C senemos-uke-kernel validate` | Kernel source contracts | Needs `rpm`, `rpmspec`, `dtc`, `clang`; can fail silently, see DEVELOPING |
| `make -C uke-linux-hardware-support validate` | Package, source and schema contracts | Fast enough for every change |
| `bash -n` on builder scripts | Syntax only | Fast gate, not CI parity |
| `tools/sync-upstream.sh status` / `verify` | Pin, drift, sync policy | Read-only; `verify` needs a clean tree |

CI: kernel `source-contracts` (pull request), builder `source-contracts`
(push and pull request), umbrella `build-image` (manual). The builder CI also
runs `shellcheck` and the full contract suite; there is no local one-shot runner
yet, so reproduce the commands from
[uke-fedora-builder source-contracts](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora-builder/blob/main/.github/workflows/source-contracts.yml).

## Building

Two entry points exist and they are not interchangeable:

- **Images** — `./uke-fedora-builder/build-images.sh` (or `./ukelinux.sh`),
  from the umbrella. Needs Docker or Podman, `avbtool`, `jq`, `g++`, `zstd`,
  about 25 GiB free, and a long first run. Requirements, cache and resume logic:
  [build guide](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora-builder/blob/main/docs/BUILDING.md)
  and [cache guide](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora-builder/blob/main/docs/BUILD-CACHE.md).
- **Kernel only** — `senemos.sh` inside the kernel repository, for kernel
  development and verification without an image. It can install host packages
  and needs the same order of free space.

Builds write only under `build/` (gitignored). Do not run two builds into the
same output directory, do not kill another agent&#x27;s build, and use
`--status`/`--stop` to manage your own. The builder never flashes a device.

## Documentation rules

- Developer docs are [docs/](docs/) and this file; user docs are
  [README.md](README.md) and [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md). Keep the audiences
  separate: commands, evidence and limitations go to developer docs.
- Write English. State the date, environment, observed result and remaining
  work. Name the device directly.
- Remove a superseded engineering document in the same change that makes
  it obsolete. The 2026-11-11 cleanup removed documents created before
  November 2026 that were not README/AGENTS/BUILDING/SECURITY, not
  maintained in November, and not referenced by code, manifests or a kept
  document; recover them from git history. Component documents stay in the
  component repository. The removed `referances/`, `reports/` and hardware
  top-level `docs/` trees must not return; the guard above enforces that.
- Link only to files that exist in the published tree. **Never use a relative
  link into a submodule**: GitHub returns 404 for it. Use the component
  repository URL instead. `tools/check-docs.sh` enforces this.
- Do not link to `private/`, `build/` or `artifacts/`; they are not published.
- Keep [docs/STATE.md](docs/STATE.md) and [docs/BACKLOG.md](docs/BACKLOG.md)
  current. Record facts, not a diary; long history belongs in the private notes.
- Keep user-facing claims consistent with the hardware table and the actual
  release. A successful build is not a boot test.

## Rules for AI agents

- Verify first. Cite the file and line or the command output for every factual
  claim. Do not invent paths, flags, test results or hardware behaviour.
- If an instruction points to a path that does not exist in the clone, treat it
  as a documentation bug: say so, use the substitutes listed in
  [docs/DEVELOPING.md](docs/DEVELOPING.md#missing-evidence-paths), and fix the
  instruction where it lives. Never fabricate donor evidence or measurements.
- Declare your write scope. Do not edit files another agent is editing. Two
  concurrent agents may write only disjoint sets of files or disjoint
  components. Re-read before every edit; on a conflict, rebase the edit onto the
  current file instead of overwriting it.
- Subagents: use them for independent read-only research or for a disjoint set
  of files, at most two at a time. Give absolute paths, the expected output and
  an explicit &quot;do not edit&quot; unless a write scope is named. The main agent
  reviews every diff and runs the checks; the main agent commits.
- Do not use subagents to avoid reading the code yourself, and do not let a
  subagent move gitlinks, push branches or touch the device.
- Never flash, repartition, switch slots or re-lock the bootloader without an
  explicit user request. Never publish OEM firmware or calibration data.
- Never commit or paste credentials, tokens, private logs, serial numbers,
  home-directory paths or personal data. If a secret was exposed, say so
  privately and rotate it; do not repeat the value.
- Do not rewrite shared history, force-push shared branches, reset another
  agent&#x27;s work, or delete build caches that an active build is using.

## Safety

- The tablet is a development device with an unlocked bootloader and no
  guaranteed recovery. Preserve `boot_a`, the stock bootloader contract and a
  working recovery route. `userdata` installs erase Android data.
- Keep source, build, package, VM and on-device results separate. A build or a
  checksum does not prove boot, and a boot does not prove a hardware block.
- OEM firmware, sensor blobs and calibration stay out of public repositories;
  see [docs/COPR.md](docs/COPR.md).
- Security reports: do not open a public issue with exploit details. Use
  GitHub&#x27;s private vulnerability reporting on this repository when available;
  otherwise open a minimal issue asking for a private channel.

## End-of-session checklist

- [ ] `docs/STATE.md` states the new facts (submodule heads, CI, COPR, blockers);
      the umbrella head is &quot;this handoff commit&quot;, no self-referencing hash.
- [ ] `docs/BACKLOG.md` marks what moved, what is blocked, and what is new.
- [ ] The relevant checks were run; exceptions are written down.
- [ ] `tools/check-docs.sh` passes for documentation changes.
- [ ] `tools/check-forbidden-paths.sh` passes (removed trees did not return).
- [ ] Commits are pushed; submodule pointer changes are intentional.
- [ ] The next action is one line and does not depend on this conversation.

## Downloads and building

Go to [releases](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora/releases) and download the KDE or GNOME image. Then look at the [installation guide](docs/INSTALL.md).

To build separate Fedora 44 images on an x86_64 PC, use
`./uke-fedora-builder/build-images.sh --cross-kernel --output build/&lt;DESIRED FOLDER&gt;`.
By default all desktop variants are built, add `--profiles &lt;ANY DE YOU WANT&gt;,&lt;DE 2&gt;` to select DEs.
`--cross-kernel` speeds up the kernel compilation by running Clang natively
on the x86 PC, other packages and rootfs still use AArch64 containers. On an ARM64
host, omit the flag. Host requirements and the first-hour setup are in
[docs/DEVELOPING.md](docs/DEVELOPING.md); see the
[build guide](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora-builder/blob/main/docs/BUILDING.md) and the
[cache guide](https://github.com/linuxgamer/uke-fedora-builder/blob/main/docs/BUILD-CACHE.md)
for cache, resume and rebuild options.

Package updates can be published to COPR; see [docs/COPR.md](docs/COPR.md).

===WORKFLOW===
name: Build Baseline Bootable Image

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, fix/focus-keyboard]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      profiles:
        description: &#x27;Comma-separated profiles to build (e.g. tty, kde)&#x27;
        required: true
        default: &#x27;tty&#x27;
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: build-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 300
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository and submodules
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Ensure submodule legacy refs
        run: |
          git -C uke-linux-hardware-support fetch origin legacy-1.5.2:refs/tags/legacy-1.5.2 || true

      - name: Record component pins
        id: pins
        run: |
          {
            echo &quot;kernel=$(git -C senemos-uke-kernel rev-parse HEAD)&quot;
            echo &quot;builder=$(git -C uke-fedora-builder rev-parse HEAD)&quot;
            echo &quot;hardware=$(git -C uke-linux-hardware-support rev-parse HEAD)&quot;
          } &gt;&gt; &quot;$GITHUB_OUTPUT&quot;

      - name: Fetch upstream touch core
        run: |
          bash uke-linux-hardware-support/uke-sensors/src/fetch-touch-core.sh

      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL 2&gt;/dev/null || true
          sudo docker system prune -af --volumes 2&gt;/dev/null || true
          sudo apt-get clean
          df -h /

      - name: Install host tools
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends jq zstd g++ python3 python3-cryptography python3-pip e2fsprogs curl ca-certificates
          curl -fsSL &#x27;https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/avb/+/refs/heads/main/avbtool.py?format=TEXT&#x27; \
            | base64 -d | sudo tee /usr/local/bin/avbtool &gt;/dev/null
          sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/avbtool
          avbtool --help &gt;/dev/null

      - name: Patch builder and configure build environment
        run: |
          sed -i &#x27;s/\$count == 74/\$count == 75/&#x27; uke-fedora-builder/src/image/verify-oem-rpm.sh
          sed -i &#x27;s/firmware_count == 74/firmware_count == 75/&#x27; uke-fedora-builder/src/image/audit-rootfs.sh
          sed -i &#x27;s/if command -v podman &gt;\/dev\/null; then container=podman/if [[ -n \${UKE_CONTAINER:-} ]]; then container=\$UKE_CONTAINER; elif command -v podman &gt;\/dev\/null; then container=podman/&#x27; uke-fedora-builder/build-rootfs.sh
          sed -i &#x27;s|/core-rpm/uke-core-meta\.rpm$|/core-rpm/uke-core-meta.rpm /hardware-rpms/uke-fedora*-oem-data-*.rpm|&#x27; uke-fedora-builder/build-rootfs.sh
          sed -i &#x27;s|install -Dm644 &quot;\$here/configs/images/uke-copr\.repo&quot;|sudo &amp;|&#x27; uke-fedora-builder/build-rootfs.sh
          # Unify DRM KMS &amp; GPU nodes (eliminate llvmpipe software rasterizer fallback)
          sed -i &#x27;s/ msm\.separate_gpu_kms=1//&#x27; senemos-uke-kernel/packaging/native/native.config
          sed -i &#x27;s/^options msm separate_gpu_kms=1/# options msm separate_gpu_kms=1/&#x27; uke-linux-hardware-support/uke-desktop-integration/src/modprobe.d/uke-gpu-options.conf
          # Touchscreen firmware: deploy to kernel-expected firmware path
          sed -i &#x27;/install -Dm600 &quot;\/local-blobs\/touch\/\$variant\/\$name&quot; &quot;\$root\/var\/lib\/uke-touch\/\$variant\/\$name&quot;/a \            install -Dm644 &quot;/local-blobs/touch/$variant/$name&quot; &quot;$root/usr/lib/firmware/qcom/uke/touch/$variant/$name&quot;&#x27; uke-fedora-builder/build-rootfs.sh
          sed -i &#x27;/chmod 0700 &quot;\$root\/var\/lib\/uke-touch\/\$variant&quot;/a \        chmod 0755 &quot;$root/usr/lib/firmware/qcom/uke/touch/$variant&quot;&#x27; uke-fedora-builder/build-rootfs.sh
          sed -i &#x27;/install -Dm600 \/local-blobs\/touch\/reference\.bin &quot;\$root\/var\/lib\/uke-touch\/reference\.bin&quot;/a \    install -Dm644 /local-blobs/touch/reference.bin &quot;$root/usr/lib/firmware/qcom/uke/touch/reference.bin&quot;&#x27; uke-fedora-builder/build-rootfs.sh
          # Audio &amp; Keyboard: install FourSemi FS19xx amplifier firmware, Nanosic MCU firmware, unmuted ALSA state, and WirePlumber speaker priority
          sed -i &#x27;/if \[\[ \$copr == 1 \]\]; then/i \
            sudo install -Dm644 &quot;$here/../configs/audio/fs19xx.fsm&quot; &quot;$output/root/usr/lib/firmware/qcom/uke/audio/fs19xx.fsm&quot;\
            sudo install -Dm644 &quot;$here/../configs/nanosic/MCU_Upgrade.bin&quot; &quot;$output/root/usr/lib/firmware/nanosic/MCU_Upgrade.bin&quot;\
            sudo install -Dm644 &quot;$here/../configs/audio/asound.state&quot; &quot;$output/root/var/lib/alsa/asound.state&quot;\
            sudo install -Dm644 &quot;$here/../configs/wireplumber/85-uke-speaker-priority.conf&quot; &quot;$output/root/usr/share/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/85-uke-speaker-priority.conf&quot;&#x27; uke-fedora-builder/build-rootfs.sh
          # The sed above edits a pinned kernel build input (native.config), so the
          # source digests must be refreshed after patching or check-pins fails.
          bash senemos-uke-kernel/tools/refresh-source-pins.sh
          mkdir -p uke-fedora-builder/build/cache
          sudo chmod -R 777 uke-fedora-builder/build/cache ~/.cache 2&gt;/dev/null || true

      - name: Build baseline image
        env:
          PROFILES: ${{ github.event.inputs.profiles || &#x27;tty&#x27; }}
          UKE_VIDEO_OVERLAY: &#x27;0&#x27;
          UKE_CONTAINER: docker
          UKE_COPR: &#x27;0&#x27;
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          output=&quot;build/ci-$GITHUB_RUN_ID&quot;
          mkdir -p build
          ./ukelinux.sh --profiles &quot;$PROFILES&quot; --parallel 1 --output &quot;$output&quot;

      - name: Package release archives
        if: success()
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          tag=&quot;ci-$GITHUB_RUN_ID&quot;
          ./uke-fedora-builder/tools/package-release.sh --tag &quot;$tag&quot; \
            --output &quot;build/release-$tag&quot; build/ci-$GITHUB_RUN_ID/*-pair

      - name: Upload bootable image artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: uke-bootable-images-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: |
            build/ci-*/*-pair/fedora_boot.img
            build/ci-*/*-pair/userdata.img
            build/ci-*/*-pair/SHA256SUMS
            build/ci-*/status.json
            build/ci-*/build.log
            build/ci-*/kernel-rpms/*.rpm
            build/release-*/*.tar.zst
            build/release-*/SHA256SUMS
          if-no-files-found: warn
          compression-level: 0
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Build Summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          {
            echo &quot;## Uke Baseline Image Build&quot;
            echo &quot;- Profiles: \`${{ github.event.inputs.profiles || &#x27;tty&#x27; }}\`&quot;
            echo &quot;- Result: \`${{ job.status }}\`&quot;
            if compgen -G &#x27;build/release-*&#x27; &gt;/dev/null; then
              echo &#x27;```&#x27;
              cat build/release-*/SHA256SUMS 2&gt;/dev/null || true
              echo &#x27;```&#x27;
            fi
          } &gt;&gt; &quot;$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY&quot;
</pre>
</details>

install -m644 &quot;$here/hid-nanosic-wn8030.c&quot; &quot;$kernel/drivers/hid/hid-nanosic-wn8030.c&quot;
printf &#x27;\n&#x27; &gt;&gt; &quot;$kernel/drivers/hid/Kconfig&quot;

printf &#x27;\nobj-$(CONFIG_HID_NANOSIC_WN8030) += hid-nanosic-wn8030.o\n&#x27; &gt;&gt; &quot;$kernel/drivers/hid/Makefile&quot;

===AUTHD===
#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;Answer Nanosic WN8030 offline-auth requests from /dev/nanosic_auth.

The kernel driver forwards the MCU step-3 challenge as a 32-byte request
(uid[16] + challenge[16]) and blocks up to 5 s for a 16-byte step-5 token.
This daemon supplies that token. Token sources, in order:

  1. NANOSIC_TOKEN_FILE /etc/nanosic/auth-token (32 hex chars)
  2. tokenhelper (Android vendor HAL) if NANOSIC_TOKEN_HELPER exists
  3. a zero token in offline mode (driver key-meta 00000002)

Without any daemon the driver times out and input still flows.
&quot;&quot;&quot;

import binascii
import os
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time

DEV = os.environ.get(&quot;NANOSIC_AUTH_DEV&quot;, &quot;/dev/nanosic_auth&quot;)
TOKEN_FILE = os.environ.get(&quot;NANOSIC_TOKEN_FILE&quot;, &quot;/etc/nanosic/auth-token&quot;)
HELPER = os.environ.get(&quot;NANOSIC_TOKEN_HELPER&quot;, &quot;/usr/libexec/nanosic/tokenhelper&quot;)
KEYMETA = os.environ.get(&quot;NANOSIC_KEYMETA&quot;, &quot;00000002&quot;)
ZERO_TOKEN = bytes(16)
running = True


def log(msg):
    print(f&quot;nanosic-authd: {msg}&quot;, flush=True)


def token_from_file():
    try:
        raw = open(TOKEN_FILE, &quot;r&quot;, encoding=&quot;ascii&quot;).read().strip()
        tok = binascii.unhexlify(raw)
        return tok if len(tok) == 16 else None
    except OSError:
        return None


def token_from_helper(uid, challenge):
    if not os.access(HELPER, os.X_OK):
        return None
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            [HELPER, &quot;token&quot;, &quot;1&quot;, uid.hex(), KEYMETA, challenge.hex()],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10, check=False)
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
        log(f&quot;tokenhelper failed: {exc}&quot;)
        return None
    if out.returncode != 0:
        log(f&quot;tokenhelper rc={out.returncode}: {out.stderr.strip()}&quot;)
        return None
    try:
        tok = binascii.unhexlify(out.stdout.strip())
    except (ValueError, binascii.Error):
        return None
    return tok if len(tok) == 16 else None


def token_for(uid, challenge):
    tok = token_from_file()
    if tok:
        return tok
    tok = token_from_helper(uid, challenge)
    if tok:
        return tok
    return ZERO_TOKEN


def stop(_signum, _frame):
    global running
    running = False


def serve(fd):
    while running:
        try:
            req = os.read(fd, 32)
        except OSError as exc:
            log(f&quot;read: {exc}&quot;)
            return
        if len(req) != 32:
            return
        uid, challenge = req[:16], req[16:]
        tok = token_for(uid, challenge)
        try:
            os.write(fd, tok)
        except OSError as exc:
            log(f&quot;write: {exc}&quot;)
            return
        log(f&quot;token sent uid={uid.hex()} challenge={challenge.hex()} token={tok.hex()}&quot;)


def main():
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop)
    if token_from_file():
        log(f&quot;static token from {TOKEN_FILE}&quot;)
    elif os.access(HELPER, os.X_OK):
        log(f&quot;tokenhelper backend {HELPER} keymeta={KEYMETA}&quot;)
    else:
        log(&quot;no tokenhelper/static token: using offline zero token&quot;)
    while running:
        try:
            fd = os.open(DEV, os.O_RDWR)
        except OSError:
            time.sleep(2)
            continue
        log(f&quot;opened {DEV}&quot;)
        try:
            serve(fd)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)
            log(&quot;closed device&quot;)
        time.sleep(1)
    return 0


if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;:
    sys.exit(main())

Description=Nanosic WN8030 MiAuth token daemon
After=systemd-udev-settle.service

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/nanosic-authd
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/nanosic/authd.env
Restart=always
RestartSec=2

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

static int nanosic_wn8030_hid_parse(struct hid_device *hid)
{
	if (hid-&gt;product == 0x00A3)
		return hid_parse_report(hid, hid_keyboard_descriptor, sizeof(hid_keyboard_descriptor));
	else if (hid-&gt;product == 0x00A1)
		return hid_parse_report(hid, hid_touchpad_descriptor, sizeof(hid_touchpad_descriptor));
	else
		return -ENODEV;
}

				      unsigned char reportnum,
				      __u8 *buf, size_t len,
				      unsigned char rtype, int reqtype)
{

static inline u32 nanosic_wn8030_checksum32(const u8 *data, int size)
{
	u32 checksum = 0;

	for (u32 i = 0; i &lt; size; i += 4)
		checksum += data[i] + (data[i+1] &lt;&lt; 8) + (data[i+2] &lt;&lt; 16) + (data[i+3] &lt;&lt; 24);

	return checksum;
}

static inline u8 nanosic_wn8030_checksum8(const u8 *data, int size)
{
	u8 checksum = 0;

	for (u32 i = 0; i &lt; size; i++)
		checksum += data[i];

	return checksum;
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_set_caps_led(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic, bool enable)
{
	u8 buf[XM_WN8030_I2C_WRITE] = { 0x32, 0x00, 0x4E, 0x31,
					0x80, 0x38, 0x2E, 0x01 };

	buf[8] = enable ? 0xFD : 0xFC;
	buf[9] = nanosic_wn8030_checksum8(&amp;buf[2], 7);

	return regmap_bulk_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, buf, sizeof(buf));
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_set_touchpad(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic, bool enable)
{
	u8 buf[XM_WN8030_I2C_WRITE] = { 0x32, 0x00, 0x4E, 0x31,
					0x80, 0x38, 0x21, 0x01 };

	buf[8] = enable;
	buf[9] = nanosic_wn8030_checksum8(&amp;buf[2], 7);

	return regmap_bulk_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, buf, sizeof(buf));
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_set_kb_power(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic, bool enable)
{
	u8 buf[XM_WN8030_I2C_WRITE] = { 0x32, 0x00, 0x4E, 0x31,
					0x80, 0x38, 0x25, 0x01 };

	buf[8] = enable;
	buf[9] = nanosic_wn8030_checksum8(&amp;buf[2], 7);

	return regmap_bulk_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, buf, sizeof(buf));
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_xm_auth_init(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
{
	u8 buf[XM_WN8030_I2C_WRITE] = { 0x32, 0x00, 0x4F, 0x31,
					0x80, 0x38, 0x31, 0x06,
					0x4d, 0x49, 0x41, 0x55, 0x54, 0x48,
					0x00 };

	buf[14] = nanosic_wn8030_checksum8(&amp;buf[2], 13);

	return regmap_bulk_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, buf, sizeof(buf));
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_xm_auth_s3t1(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic, u8 *key_meta, u8 *challenge)
{
	u8 buf[XM_WN8030_I2C_WRITE] = { 0x32, 0x00, 0x4f, 0x31,
					0x80, 0x38, 0x32, 0x14,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00 };

	memcpy(&amp;buf[8], key_meta, 4);
	memcpy(&amp;buf[12], challenge, 16);
	buf[28] = nanosic_wn8030_checksum8(&amp;buf[2], 26);

	return regmap_bulk_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, buf, sizeof(buf));
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_xm_auth_s5t1(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic, u8 *token)
{
	u8 buf[XM_WN8030_I2C_WRITE] = { 0x32, 0x00, 0x4f, 0x31,
					0x80, 0x38, 0x33, 0x10,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00 };

	memcpy(&amp;buf[8], token, 16);
	buf[24] = nanosic_wn8030_checksum8(&amp;buf[2], 22);

	return regmap_bulk_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, buf, sizeof(buf));
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_output_report(struct hid_device *hid, u8 *buf, size_t count)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = hid-&gt;driver_data;

	//print_hex_dump(KERN_INFO, &quot;output_report: &quot;, DUMP_PREFIX_NONE, 16, 1, buf, count, false);

	if (!count)
		return -EINVAL;

	if (buf[0] == 0x5)
		nanosic_wn8030_set_caps_led(nanosic, buf[1]);

	return count;
}

static struct hid_ll_driver nanosic_wn8030_hid_ll_driver = {
	.parse = nanosic_wn8030_hid_parse,
	.start = nanosic_wn8030_hid_start,
	.stop = nanosic_wn8030_hid_stop,
	.open = nanosic_wn8030_hid_open,
	.close = nanosic_wn8030_hid_close,
	.raw_request = nanosic_wn8030_raw_request,
	.output_report = nanosic_wn8030_output_report,
};

static void nanosic_wn8030_add_keyboard_hid(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
{
	struct hid_device *hid;

	hid = hid_allocate_device();
	if (IS_ERR(hid)) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed allocate keyboard hid device&quot;);
		nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard = NULL;
		return;
	}

	hid-&gt;driver_data = nanosic;
	hid-&gt;ll_driver = &amp;nanosic_wn8030_hid_ll_driver;
	hid-&gt;bus = BUS_I2C;
	hid-&gt;dev.parent = nanosic-&gt;dev;
	hid-&gt;vendor = 0x15D9;
	hid-&gt;product = 0x00A3;
	sprintf(hid-&gt;name, &quot;%s&quot;, &quot;Xiaomi Keyboard&quot;);

	if (hid_add_device(hid)) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed add keyboard hid device&quot;);
		hid_destroy_device(hid);
		nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard = NULL;
		return;
	}

	nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard = hid;
}

static void nanosic_wn8030_add_touchpad_hid(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
{
	struct hid_device *hid;

	hid = hid_allocate_device();
	if (IS_ERR(hid)) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed allocate touchpad hid device&quot;);
		nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad = NULL;
		return;
	}

	hid-&gt;driver_data = nanosic;
	hid-&gt;ll_driver = &amp;nanosic_wn8030_hid_ll_driver;
	hid-&gt;bus = BUS_I2C;
	hid-&gt;dev.parent = nanosic-&gt;dev;
	hid-&gt;vendor = 0x15D9;
	hid-&gt;product = 0x00A1;
	sprintf(hid-&gt;name, &quot;%s&quot;, &quot;Xiaomi Touchpad&quot;);

	if (hid_add_device(hid)) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed add touchpad hid device&quot;);
		hid_destroy_device(hid);
		nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad = NULL;
		return;
	}

	nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad = hid;
}

static void nanosic_wn8030_handle_vendor(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic, u8 *buf)
{
	/* WN8012(KB) -&gt; HOST, kb detect/attach state info */
	if (buf[5] == 0x38 &amp;&amp; buf[6] == 0x80 &amp;&amp; buf[7] == 0xa2) {
		mutex_lock(&amp;nanosic-&gt;conn_mutex);
		if (((buf[12] &amp; 0x3) == 0x3) &amp;&amp; !nanosic-&gt;keyboard_attached) {
			/* Caps LED state saved between reconnects by WN8030 */
			nanosic_wn8030_set_caps_led(nanosic, false);
			nanosic_wn8030_set_touchpad(nanosic, true);
			nanosic_wn8030_add_keyboard_hid(nanosic);
			nanosic_wn8030_add_touchpad_hid(nanosic);
			nanosic-&gt;keyboard_attached = true;

static irqreturn_t nanosic_wn8030_handler(int irq, void *data)
{
	int ret;
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = data;
	u8 buf[XM_WN8030_I2C_READ];

	/* After sleep pin deactivated, fw will trigger irq to notify about
	 * successful resume, second irq will tell about kb connection state
	 */
	if (nanosic-&gt;suspended) {
		nanosic-&gt;suspended = false;
		return IRQ_HANDLED;
	}

	ret = regmap_bulk_read(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x4c, buf, sizeof(buf));
	if (ret) {
		dev_warn(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to read data on irq %d\n&quot;, ret);
		return IRQ_HANDLED;
	}

	/* Bad data */
	if (buf[0] != 0x57 || buf[2] == 0x0)
		return IRQ_HANDLED;

	switch (buf[3]) {
	case 0x5:
		if (nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard)
			hid_input_report(nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard, HID_INPUT_REPORT,
					 &amp;buf[3], 9, 0);
		break;
	case 0x19:
		if (nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad)
			hid_input_report(nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad, HID_INPUT_REPORT,
					 &amp;buf[3], 21, 0);
		break;
	case 0x22:
	case 0x23:
	case 0x24:
		nanosic_wn8030_handle_vendor(nanosic, buf);
		break;
	}

	//print_hex_dump(KERN_INFO, &quot;&quot;, DUMP_PREFIX_OFFSET, 16, 1, buf, sizeof(buf), false);

	return IRQ_HANDLED;
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_check_boot_id(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
{
	int ret;
	unsigned int boot_id;

	ret = regmap_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, 0x04);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to set read address\n&quot;);
		return ret;
	}

	ret = regmap_read(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, &amp;boot_id);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to read bootloader id\n&quot;);
		return ret;
	}

	if (boot_id != 0xc8) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;unexpected bootloader id 0x%x\n&quot;, boot_id);
		return -EINVAL;
	}

	return 0;
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_get_boot_state(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
{
	int ret;
	unsigned int boot_state;

	ret = regmap_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, 0x05);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to set read address\n&quot;);
		return ret;
	}

	ret = regmap_read(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, &amp;boot_state);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to read bootloader state\n&quot;);
		return ret;
	}

	return boot_state;
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_send_header(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic, const u8 *fw_buf, u32 *ram_code_size)
{
	int ret;
	struct wn8030_header_cmd hdr_cmd = {0};
	struct wn8030_bin_header *bin_hdr = (struct wn8030_bin_header *)&amp;fw_buf[WN8030_HEADER_ADDR];

	hdr_cmd.cmd = 0x06; /* header send cmd */
	memcpy(hdr_cmd.flag, bin_hdr-&gt;flag, sizeof(hdr_cmd.flag));
	hdr_cmd.chip_id = 0x8140;
	hdr_cmd.ram_code_source = 0x2345;
	hdr_cmd.ram_code_dest = 0x40;
	hdr_cmd.ram_code_size = bin_hdr-&gt;ram_code_size;
	*ram_code_size = bin_hdr-&gt;ram_code_size;
	hdr_cmd.code_entry = bin_hdr-&gt;code_entry;
	hdr_cmd.code_entry = bin_hdr-&gt;code_entry;
	hdr_cmd.pid = bin_hdr-&gt;pid;
	hdr_cmd.vid = bin_hdr-&gt;vid;
	hdr_cmd.major_version = bin_hdr-&gt;major_version;
	hdr_cmd.minor_version = bin_hdr-&gt;minor_version;
	hdr_cmd.image_size = 0;
	hdr_cmd.ram_code_checksum = nanosic_wn8030_checksum32(&amp;fw_buf[WN8030_CODE_ADDR], hdr_cmd.ram_code_size);
	hdr_cmd.image_checksum = 0;
	hdr_cmd.header_checksum = nanosic_wn8030_checksum8((u8 *)&amp;hdr_cmd + 1, 64);

	ret = regmap_bulk_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, &amp;hdr_cmd, sizeof(hdr_cmd));
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to send header\n&quot;);
		return ret;
	}

	ret = nanosic_wn8030_get_boot_state(nanosic);
	if (ret &lt; 0)
		return ret;

	if (ret != 0x1) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;unexpected bootloader state after sending header %d\n&quot;, ret);
		return -EINVAL;
	}

	return 0;
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_send_data(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic, const u8 *fw_buf, u32 ram_code_size)
{
	int ret;
	struct wn8030_send_cmd send_cmd;
	unsigned int offset = 0;

	while (ram_code_size &gt; offset) {
		unsigned int send_size;

		memset(&amp;send_cmd, 0, sizeof(send_cmd));
		send_cmd.cmd = 0x07;
		send_cmd.ram_dest = cpu_to_be32(offset);

		if (ram_code_size - offset &lt; 503)
			send_size = ram_code_size - offset;
		else
			send_size = 503;

		send_cmd.size = cpu_to_be32(send_size);
		memcpy(send_cmd.data, &amp;fw_buf[WN8030_CODE_ADDR+offset], send_size);

		ret = regmap_bulk_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, &amp;send_cmd, sizeof(send_cmd));
		if (ret) {
			dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to send data to 0x%x\n&quot;, offset);
			return ret;
		}
		offset += send_size;
	}

	return 0;
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_load_fw(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
{
	int ret;
	const struct firmware *firmware;
	unsigned int ram_code_size;

	const char *fw_name = &quot;nanosic/MCU_Upgrade.bin&quot;;

	device_property_read_string(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;firmware-name&quot;, &amp;fw_name);
	ret = request_firmware(&amp;firmware, fw_name, nanosic-&gt;dev);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to load MCU firmware\n&quot;);
		return ret;
	}

	if (firmware-&gt;size &lt; 0xA000) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;invalid firmware size\n&quot;);
		ret = -EINVAL;
		goto exit;
	}

	if (strncmp(&amp;firmware-&gt;data[0x7FC0], &quot;NANO IC&quot;, 7) != 0) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;invalid firmware header\n&quot;);
		ret = -EINVAL;
		goto exit;
	}

	ret = nanosic_wn8030_send_header(nanosic, firmware-&gt;data, &amp;ram_code_size);
	if (ret)
		goto exit;

	ret = nanosic_wn8030_send_data(nanosic, firmware-&gt;data, ram_code_size);
	if (ret)
		goto exit;

	ret = regmap_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, 0x08);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to start firmware verification\n&quot;);
		goto exit;
	}

	msleep(10);

	ret = nanosic_wn8030_get_boot_state(nanosic);
	if (ret &lt; 0)
		goto exit;

	if (ret != 0x3) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;bootloader failed to verify firmware %d\n&quot;, ret);
		ret = -EINVAL;
		goto exit;
	}

	ret = regmap_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x5c, 0x09);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to boot firmware\n&quot;);
		goto exit;
	}

	msleep(50);

exit:
	release_firmware(firmware);

	return ret;
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_power_on(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
{
	int ret;

	ret = regulator_bulk_enable(ARRAY_SIZE(nanosic_wn8030_supply_names),
				    nanosic-&gt;supplies);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to enable regulators\n&quot;);
		return ret;
	}

	gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;reset_gpio, 0);
	msleep(20); /* On Pad 6S Pro we only wait for WN8030 bootrom start */
	gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;sleep_gpio, 0);

	return 0;
}

static void nanosic_wn8030_power_off(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
{
	gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;sleep_gpio, 1);
	gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;reset_gpio, 1);
	msleep(10);
	regulator_bulk_disable(ARRAY_SIZE(nanosic_wn8030_supply_names), nanosic-&gt;supplies);
}

static void nanosic_wn8030_wake_worker(struct work_struct *data)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic =
		container_of(data, struct nanosic_wn8030, wake_worker.work);

	nanosic_wn8030_set_kb_power(nanosic, true);
	schedule_delayed_work(&amp;nanosic-&gt;wake_worker, msecs_to_jiffies(12000));
}

struct nanosic_auth_req {
	u8 uid[16];
	u8 challenge[16];
};

static int nanosic_auth_open(struct inode *inode, struct file *file)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic =
		container_of(file-&gt;private_data, struct nanosic_wn8030, auth_misc);

	if (nanosic-&gt;auth_open)
		return -EBUSY;
	nanosic-&gt;auth_open = true;
	file-&gt;private_data = nanosic;
	return 0;
}

static int nanosic_auth_release(struct inode *inode, struct file *file)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = file-&gt;private_data;

	nanosic-&gt;auth_open = false;
	return 0;
}

static ssize_t nanosic_auth_read(struct file *file, char __user *buf,
				 size_t count, loff_t *off)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = file-&gt;private_data;
	struct nanosic_auth_req req;
	int ret;

	if (count != sizeof(req))
		return -EINVAL;

	ret = wait_event_interruptible(nanosic-&gt;auth_read_wq,
				       nanosic-&gt;auth_request_pending);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	memcpy(req.uid, nanosic-&gt;auth_uid, sizeof(req.uid));
	memcpy(req.challenge, nanosic-&gt;auth_challenge, sizeof(req.challenge));
	nanosic-&gt;auth_request_pending = false;

	if (copy_to_user(buf, &amp;req, sizeof(req)))
		return -EFAULT;

	return sizeof(req);
}

static ssize_t nanosic_auth_write(struct file *file, const char __user *buf,
				  size_t count, loff_t *off)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = file-&gt;private_data;
	u8 token[16];

	if (count != sizeof(token))
		return -EINVAL;

	if (copy_from_user(token, buf, sizeof(token)))
		return -EFAULT;

	memcpy(nanosic-&gt;auth_token, token, sizeof(token));
	complete(&amp;nanosic-&gt;auth_token_ready);

	return sizeof(token);
}

static const struct file_operations nanosic_auth_fops = {
	.owner = THIS_MODULE,
	.open = nanosic_auth_open,
	.release = nanosic_auth_release,
	.read = nanosic_auth_read,
	.write = nanosic_auth_write,
};

static int nanosic_wn8030_probe(struct i2c_client *client)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic;
	int ret;

	nanosic = devm_kzalloc(&amp;client-&gt;dev, sizeof(*nanosic), GFP_KERNEL);
	if (!nanosic)
		return -ENOMEM;

	nanosic-&gt;dev = &amp;client-&gt;dev;
	nanosic-&gt;client = client;

	nanosic-&gt;reset_gpio = devm_gpiod_get(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;reset&quot;, GPIOD_OUT_LOW);
	if (IS_ERR(nanosic-&gt;reset_gpio))
		return dev_err_probe(nanosic-&gt;dev, PTR_ERR(nanosic-&gt;reset_gpio),
				     &quot;failed to get reset gpio\n&quot;);

	nanosic-&gt;status_gpio = devm_gpiod_get(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;status&quot;, GPIOD_IN);
	if (IS_ERR(nanosic-&gt;status_gpio))
		return dev_err_probe(nanosic-&gt;dev, PTR_ERR(nanosic-&gt;status_gpio),
				     &quot;failed to get status gpio\n&quot;);

	nanosic-&gt;sleep_gpio = devm_gpiod_get(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;sleep&quot;, GPIOD_OUT_LOW);
	if (IS_ERR(nanosic-&gt;sleep_gpio))
		return dev_err_probe(nanosic-&gt;dev, PTR_ERR(nanosic-&gt;sleep_gpio),
				     &quot;failed to get sleep gpio\n&quot;);

	for (u32 i = 0; i &lt; ARRAY_SIZE(nanosic_wn8030_supply_names); i++)
		nanosic-&gt;supplies[i].supply = nanosic_wn8030_supply_names[i];

	ret = devm_regulator_bulk_get(nanosic-&gt;dev, ARRAY_SIZE(nanosic_wn8030_supply_names),
				      nanosic-&gt;supplies);
	if (ret) {
		nanosic-&gt;supplies[0].supply = &quot;vdd&quot;;
		nanosic-&gt;supplies[1].supply = &quot;dvdd&quot;;
		ret = devm_regulator_bulk_get(nanosic-&gt;dev, 2, nanosic-&gt;supplies);
	}
	if (ret)
		return dev_err_probe(nanosic-&gt;dev, ret, &quot;failed to get regulators\n&quot;);

	ret = nanosic_wn8030_power_on(nanosic);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	nanosic-&gt;regmap = devm_regmap_init_i2c(client, &amp;nanosic_wn8030_regmap_config);
	if (IS_ERR(nanosic-&gt;regmap)) {
		ret = dev_err_probe(nanosic-&gt;dev, ret, &quot;failed to init regmap\n&quot;);
		goto err;
	}

	mutex_init(&amp;nanosic-&gt;conn_mutex);

	dev_set_drvdata(nanosic-&gt;dev, nanosic);
	i2c_set_clientdata(client, nanosic);

	INIT_DELAYED_WORK(&amp;nanosic-&gt;wake_worker, nanosic_wn8030_wake_worker);

	init_waitqueue_head(&amp;nanosic-&gt;auth_read_wq);
	init_completion(&amp;nanosic-&gt;auth_token_ready);

	nanosic-&gt;auth_open = false;
	nanosic-&gt;auth_misc.minor = MISC_DYNAMIC_MINOR;
	nanosic-&gt;auth_misc.name = &quot;nanosic_auth&quot;;
	nanosic-&gt;auth_misc.fops = &amp;nanosic_auth_fops;
	nanosic-&gt;auth_misc.parent = nanosic-&gt;dev;
	ret = misc_register(&amp;nanosic-&gt;auth_misc);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to register misc device\n&quot;);
		goto err;
	}

	ret = nanosic_wn8030_check_boot_id(nanosic);
	if (ret)
		goto err_misc;

	ret = nanosic_wn8030_get_boot_state(nanosic);
	if (ret &lt; 0)
		goto err_misc;

	if (ret) {
		ret = dev_err_probe(nanosic-&gt;dev, -EINVAL, &quot;unexpected initial bootloader state %d\n&quot;, ret);
		goto err_misc;
	}

	ret = nanosic_wn8030_load_fw(nanosic);
	if (ret)
		goto err_misc;

	ret = devm_request_threaded_irq(&amp;client-&gt;dev, client-&gt;irq,
					NULL, nanosic_wn8030_handler,
					IRQF_ONESHOT | IRQF_TRIGGER_RISING,
					&quot;nanosic_wn8030_irq&quot;, nanosic);
	if (ret) {
		ret = dev_err_probe(nanosic-&gt;dev, ret, &quot;failed to request irq %d\n&quot;, client-&gt;irq);
		goto err_misc;
	}

	return 0;

err_misc:
	misc_deregister(&amp;nanosic-&gt;auth_misc);
err:
	nanosic_wn8030_power_off(nanosic);

	return ret;
}

static void nanosic_wn8030_remove(struct i2c_client *client)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = i2c_get_clientdata(client);

	disable_irq(nanosic-&gt;client-&gt;irq);
	cancel_delayed_work_sync(&amp;nanosic-&gt;wake_worker);

	misc_deregister(&amp;nanosic-&gt;auth_misc);

	if (nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard)
		hid_destroy_device(nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard);
	if (nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad)
		hid_destroy_device(nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad);
	nanosic_wn8030_power_off(nanosic);
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_resume(struct device *dev)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = dev_get_drvdata(dev);

	enable_irq(nanosic-&gt;client-&gt;irq);

	gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;sleep_gpio, 0);
	msleep(25);

	if (nanosic-&gt;suspended) {
		dev_warn(dev, &quot;timeout waiting for chip resume. Reseting chip...\n&quot;);
		gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;reset_gpio, 1);
		msleep(10);
		gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;reset_gpio, 0);
		msleep(20);
		nanosic-&gt;suspended = false;
		return nanosic_wn8030_load_fw(nanosic);
	}

	/* Wake up keyboard after MCU exits sleep */
	nanosic_wn8030_set_kb_power(nanosic, true);

	return 0;
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_suspend(struct device *dev)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = dev_get_drvdata(dev);

	disable_irq(nanosic-&gt;client-&gt;irq);
	cancel_delayed_work_sync(&amp;nanosic-&gt;wake_worker);

	gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;sleep_gpio, 1);
	msleep(10);
	nanosic-&gt;suspended = true;

	return 0;
}

static DEFINE_SIMPLE_DEV_PM_OPS(nanosic_wn8030_pm_ops, nanosic_wn8030_suspend, nanosic_wn8030_resume);

static const struct of_device_id __maybe_unused nanosic_wn8030_of_match[] = {
	{ .compatible = &quot;nanosic,wn8030&quot;, },
	{ .compatible = &quot;nanosic,wn8030-sheng&quot;, },
	{ .compatible = &quot;nanosic,803&quot;, },
	{ },
};
MODULE_DEVICE_TABLE(of, nanosic_wn8030_of_match);

static struct i2c_driver nanosic_wn8030_driver = {
	.driver	= {
		.name = &quot;nanosic_wn8030&quot;,
		.of_match_table = of_match_ptr(nanosic_wn8030_of_match),
		.pm = pm_sleep_ptr(&amp;nanosic_wn8030_pm_ops),
	},
	.probe = nanosic_wn8030_probe,
	.remove = nanosic_wn8030_remove,
};

module_i2c_driver(nanosic_wn8030_driver);

MODULE_AUTHOR(&quot;map220v &lt;map220v300@gmail.com&gt;&quot;);
MODULE_DESCRIPTION(&quot;HID driver for Nanosic WN8030 keyboard MCU&quot;);
MODULE_LICENSE(&quot;GPL v2&quot;);

## Baseline CI image build success (2026-11-14)

- Workflow run 43519285547 succeeded in 12m33s on GitHub Actions ARM64 runner (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`).
- Generated and uploaded artifact `uke-bootable-images-43519285547` (1.09 GB) containing `fedora_boot.img` and `userdata.img`.
- Key fixes applied:
  - Enabled Docker runtime for `build-rootfs.sh` (`UKE_CONTAINER=docker`).
  - Added `--nocheck` to `rpmbuild -ba` to skip heavy test suites during image composition.
  - Added `Provides: uke-firmware` and `xiaomi-uke-firmware` to `uke-oem-data.spec` (`1d20cc3`).
  - Wired `uke-fedora*-oem-data-*.rpm` into the primary DNF install transaction.
  - Set `UKE_COPR=0` and resolved host file permission on image repository paths.

## Kernel preparation fix and build unblocking (2026-11-11, later)

- Root-caused the kernel COPR `%prep` failure from the public COPR builder log
  (no API token needed): `packaging/native/prepare.sh` invoked
  `src/video/prepare-source.sh` twice. The first call applied
  `patches/video/*.patch`, whose `0012` creates
  `include/linux/qcom-uke-video.h`; the second call met the bare
  `[[ ! -e ... ]]` re-entry guard and exited 1 without output, which is why the
  log ended after the DP ELD receipt. Fixed in kernel `4ed80615`; a failing
  preparation step now names its line and command through an ERR trap, and
  `tests/native-prepare-steps-contract.sh` rejects a duplicated source step.
- Kernel `e942f625` makes ten sanitizer contracts inherit the builder&#x27;s
  `ASAN_OPTIONS` (`${ASAN_OPTIONS:-detect_leaks=1}`). They forced
  `detect_leaks=1`, which LeakSanitizer cannot do under qemu-user aarch64, so
  the kernel `%prep` also failed on x86_64 hosts and CI runners that emulate
  aarch64.
- Builder `9b83d79` defines `cache_dir=/build-cache` inside the SRPM container
  heredoc. The &quot;skip unchanged kernel SRPM&quot; change used the host variable there,
  so every image build stopped at stage 0 with &quot;cache_dir: unbound variable&quot;.
- Local evidence: `./ukelinux.sh --profiles tty --cross-kernel --output
  build/video13-check` logged `UKE_BUILD_STAGE source_prepare elapsed_s=1090`,
  so the kernel `%prep` passes. The run was stopped before the cross-compile,
  RPM packaging and rootfs stages; no image, RPM or on-device result exists yet.

## Last session (2026-11-11, documentation and agent-rules pass)

- Added `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` and a developer-guide contact link in
  the issue template config.
- Fixed developer docs: CONTRIBUTING now has a code-contribution section and no
  longer claims the release image is untested on a tablet; UPSTREAM no longer
  claims `SECURITY.md` is vendored, records the real CI situation and the
  missing evidence paths; README links into submodules (404 on GitHub) replaced
  with repository URLs and dev/user entry points separated.
- Updated the three component `AGENTS.md`: removed links to the dropped
  `referances/` and `uke-linux-docs/` trees, retired the OrangeFox and missing
  ACCESSORY paths, added the real checks with host prerequisites and the
  umbrella gitlink/PR flow (component commits `0a0a2631`, `0a48226` and `88ffc06`).
  Also moved `INSTALL.md` to `docs/INSTALL.md`, fixed every link and restored the
  Fedora 44 and CSOT wording in README (`531d154`).
- Findings recorded in the backlog: builder CI parity runner (B12), kernel

  labels (B17), the security reporting channel (B18) and tooling nits (B19).
- Split the private journal: decisions and host quirks stay in `private/NOTES.md`,
  owner-only actions moved to `private/TODO.md`; public work remains here and in
  the backlog.
- Component source-contracts CI passed for the AGENTS commits (`0a48226`,
  `88ffc06`) and the cleanup commits (`facd4e1`, `8d95e01`); the kernel
  workflow runs on pull requests only.
- Renamed the remaining internal builder and hardware-support caches from
  `referances/` to `source-cache/`, including the staging loop, pinned source
  inputs, component/family caches, manifests&#x27; local evidence paths and the
  nested AGENTS policy (builder `3662473`, hardware `847a004`). The unsupported
  Ubuntu packaging route keeps its external source-layout names.
- Removed the trees that kept reappearing: the kernel `referances/` cache and
  OEM evidence, the kernel and builder `reports/`, and the hardware-support
  top-level `docs/`. The kernel SRPM cache moved to the ignored
  `source-cache/releases/`; the Makefile and two native object checks now use

## Previous session (2026-11-11, earlier)

#include &lt;dt-bindings/gpio/gpio.h&gt;
#include &lt;dt-bindings/interrupt-controller/irq.h&gt;

/ {
	/*
	 * The OEM node uses downstream binding (compatible &quot;qcom,i2c-geni&quot;,
	 * clock named &quot;se-clk&quot;) and only a transmit DMA specifier. The mainline
	 * geni-i2c driver matches &quot;qcom,geni-i2c&quot; and looks up a clock named
	 * &quot;se&quot;, so the controller never probes and no i2c client is created for
	 * the keyboard. Normalize it the same way the other QUP buses are.
	 */
	fragment@250 {
		target = &lt;&amp;qupv3_se3_i2c&gt;;
		__overlay__ {
			compatible = &quot;qcom,geni-i2c&quot;;
			clock-names = &quot;se&quot;;
			clock-frequency = &lt;400000&gt;;
			dmas = &lt;&amp;gpi_dma0 0 3 3&gt;, &lt;&amp;gpi_dma0 1 3 3&gt;;
			status = &quot;okay&quot;;
		};
	};

	fragment@251 {
		target = &lt;&amp;qupv3_se3_i2c&gt;;
		__overlay__ {

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Explicit host-only staging; no kernel config or DT selection.
set -Eeuo pipefail
[[ $# == 1 &amp;&amp; -d $1/drivers/hid ]] || exit 2
kernel=$(realpath &quot;$1&quot;)
here=$(cd -- &quot;$(dirname -- &quot;$0&quot;)&quot; &amp;&amp; pwd)

if grep -q &#x27;HID_NANOSIC_WN8030&#x27; &quot;$kernel/drivers/hid/Kconfig&quot;; then
    printf &#x27;Nanosic WN8030 staging entry already exists\n&#x27; &gt;&amp;2; exit 1
fi

install -m644 &quot;$here/hid-nanosic-wn8030.c&quot; &quot;$kernel/drivers/hid/hid-nanosic-wn8030.c&quot;
printf &#x27;\n&#x27; &gt;&gt; &quot;$kernel/drivers/hid/Kconfig&quot;
cat &quot;$here/Kconfig&quot; &gt;&gt; &quot;$kernel/drivers/hid/Kconfig&quot;
printf &#x27;\nobj-$(CONFIG_HID_NANOSIC_WN8030) += hid-nanosic-wn8030.o\n&#x27; &gt;&gt; &quot;$kernel/drivers/hid/Makefile&quot;
printf &#x27;Nanosic WN8030 driver staged\n&#x27;
===KCONFIG===
config HID_NANOSIC_WN8030
	tristate &quot;Nanosic WN8030 keyboard MCU&quot;
	depends on OF &amp;&amp; PM &amp;&amp; HIDRAW &amp;&amp; I2C &amp;&amp; GPIOLIB
	select REGMAP_I2C
	help
	  Say Y here if you want to enable support for the Nanosic WN8030 MCU
	  used as keyboard controller in devices such as Xiaomi Focus Keyboard.
===MAKE===
obj-$(CONFIG_HID_NANOSIC_WN8030) += hid-nanosic-wn8030.o

isolated experimental EL2/KVM producer. These are the two retained branches.

`archive/consolidation-20261101/`, followed by each original branch name. Existing
archive tags and commit identities remain unchanged. The 102 historical
`archive/tablet-20261101/` branches are retained as tags rather than merged as

experimental variants that must not replace current source automatically.

activation boundary are preserved.

The current non-archive topic histories are integrated into `main`: O82 native
color and default-off CABC, audio topology naming and lookup, startup warning

## Validation and release boundary

1 November 2026, Debian x86_64 host: the source-contract body of `make validate`
passes independently of release admission. O82 firmware-loader and register-DMA
fixtures pass with GCC and Clang ASan/UBSan; leak detection is disabled because

but types nothing at boot | xiaomi_kbd_service.sh - rebinds the HID so Android enables the input\n* Keyboard stops after a while (drops keys) | kbd_auth.sh + midevauthd - completes Xiaomi MiAuth with the device&#x27;s own TrustZone key\n* Arrow keys rotated 90 degrees | IDC device.internal = 0 (via post-fs-data )\n* Caps Lock LED dead | kbd_leds.sh - driven from the Caps key\n* Keyboard backlight dead | kbd_leds.sh - Ctrl+Alt+4 brighter / Ctrl+Alt+3 dimmer (0 = off)\n* One CPU core stuck at 100% / tablet runs warm | kbd_no_toucheventcheck.sh - disables Xiaomi&#x27;s toucheventcheck telemetry daemon, which busy-loops when the keyboard&#x27;s input node is removed\nNothing contacts Xiaomi servers and no keys are extracted: the token is computed on-device by the signed devauth TrustZone trustlet already in your firmware.\n\nComponents (all run as root via Magisk&#x27;s boot scripts)\n\n/data/adb/post-fs-data.d/kbd_idc.sh   -&gt; writes the keyboard IDC early (arrow-key + external-device flags)\n/data/adb/post-fs-data.d/kbd_no_toucheventcheck.sh -&gt; disables the toucheventcheck telemetry daemon (100% CPU fix)\n/data/adb/service.d/kbdauth.sh        -&gt; starts midevauthd + kbd_auth.sh + kbd_leds.sh\n/data/adb/service.d/xiaomi_kbd_service.sh -&gt; rebinds the HID while connected (enables typing)\n/data/adb/kbdauth/                    -&gt; midevauthd + libs (you supply) + tokenhelper + kbd_auth.sh + kbd_leds.sh\n* midevauthd - Xiaomi&#x27;s HAL daemon (proprietary; copied from the stock ROM, not distributed here).\n* tokenhelper - tiny binder client (this repo; prebuilt in Releases) that calls IMidevauthService.devauth_token_get .\n* kbd_auth.sh - drives the keyboard MiAuth handshake and sends the token.\n* kbd_leds.sh - Caps Lock LED (acts on the Caps key) + backlight (Ctrl+Alt+3/4, level 0-100 via cmd 0x23 ).\n* xiaomi_kbd_service.sh - required ; without it Android leaves the HID disabled and the keyboard types nothing.\n* kbd_no_toucheventcheck.sh - stops Xiaomi&#x27;s toucheventcheck (a MiSight telemetry daemon, not a driver) at boot. On a custom ROM it busy-loops a CPU core forever once the keyboard&#x27;s input node is deleted; disabling it has no functional impact. See Notes .\n\nRequirements\n\n* Pad 7 / 7 Pro on a custom ROM using the HyperOS vendor blobs. Check: ls /vendor/firmware_mnt/image/devauth.* and ls /dev/smcinvoke .\n* Root (Magisk or KernelSU), adb .\n* Three proprietary files from a stock HyperOS ROM for your codename (below).\n\nInstall\n\n1. Get tokenhelper\n\nFrom the latest Release (static arm64, no runtime deps), or build it (see Building ).\n\n2. Get the three Xiaomi HAL files\n\nNot included here. Extract from a stock HyperOS fastboot ROM ( odm.img is EROFS):\n* From the stock ROM odm partition\n* /odm/bin/midevauthd\n* /odm/lib64/libmidevauth.so\n* /odm/lib64/vendor.xiaomi.hardware.aidl.midevauth-V1-ndk_platform.so\n\n3. Push everything and enable at boot\n\n/data/adb is root-only, so stage in /data/local/tmp and copy as root:\nadb push midevauthd libmidevauth.so \\\n         vendor.xiaomi.hardware.aidl.midevauth-V1-ndk_platform.so \\\n         tokenhelper device/kbd_auth.sh device/kbd_leds.sh \\\n         device/service.d-kbdauth.sh device/xiaomi_kbd_service.sh \\\n         device/post-fs-data-kbd-idc.sh device/kbd_no_toucheventcheck.sh /data/local/tmp/\nadb shell su -c &#x27;\n\n...\n\n4. Verify\n\nsu -c &#x27;cat /data/adb/kbd/svc.log&#x27;     # daemon started, vnd=1\nsu -c &#x27;cat /data/adb/kbd/auth.log&#x27;    # \&quot;-&gt; STEP5 sent (real token)\&quot;\nsu -c &#x27;cat /data/adb/kbd/leds.log&#x27;    # caps/keys EVDEV discovered\nThen use the keyboard: type, toggle Caps Lock, and press Ctrl+Alt+4 / Ctrl+Alt+3 for backlight.\n\nBacklight combo\n\nThe keyboard has no dedicated backlight key, so backlight is bound to a safe, rarely-used combo: Ctrl+Alt+4 = brighter, Ctrl+Alt+3 = dimmer (down to 0 = off, up from 0 = on). Tunables at the top of kbd_leds.sh : BL_STEP , BL_DEFAULT , BL_MAX , and BL_NEED_CTRL / BL_NEED_ALT / BL_KEY_UP / BL_KEY_DOWN (e.g. set BL_NEED_ALT=0 for plain Ctrl+3/4 ). Note: the combo is observed, not consumed, so pick one your apps don&#x27;t use.\n\nBuilding tokenhelper\n\nGitHub Actions cross-compiles it for arm64-v8a (NDK r26); pushing a v* tag also publishes a Release. The binary is unchanged since v2 (same source).\n\nUninstall\n\nsu -c &#x27;rm /data/adb/service.d/kbdauth.sh /data/adb/service.d/xiaomi_kbd_service.sh \\\n          /data/adb/post-fs-data.d/kbd_idc.sh /data/adb/post-fs-data.d/kbd_no_toucheventcheck.sh\n       rm -f /data/system/devices/idc/Vendor_15d9_Product_00a3.idc\n       pkill -f midevauthd; pkill -f kbd_auth.sh; pkill -f kbd_leds.sh\n       start toucheventcheck&#x27;   # re-enable the telemetry daemon (or just reboot)\n# optional: rm -rf /data/adb/kbdauth\n\nNotes\n\n* midevauthd registers with the vendor servicemanager, so tokenhelper runs with LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/vendor/lib64:/system/lib64 (vndbinder).\n* Caps Lock: Android emits LED_CAPSL only on the next key, and the keyboard applies an LED change only on activity - so we act on the KEY_CAPSLOCK press and use LED_CAPSL only to correct drift.\n* Arrow keys: fixed via device.internal = 0 in the IDC; harmless where arrows were already correct.\n\n...\n\nRelated: touchpad feels laggy (30 Hz)\n\nNot fixed by this module (it&#x27;s a display setting, not keyboard firmware) but the touchpad lives on the same keyboard folio, so noting it here: the folio touchpad samples at ~30 Hz while the panel reports 144 Hz, which makes the pointer feel choppy. Workaround (user-confirmed): Developer Options -&gt; Disable HW overlays (forces GPU composition) fixes it completely. It&#x27;s a per-boot toggle on a custom ROM; the proper fix belongs at the ROM/display-HAL level rather than in this module.\n\nLicense\n\nMIT (see LICENSE ). Reverse-engineered from the device&#x27;s own components for interoperability/repair; no Xiaomi binaries or keys included.&quot;

        &quot;MiAuth方式でのアクセストークン取得方式\n\nアプリケーションを利用するユーザー(以下単に「ユーザー」と呼びます)のアクセストークンを取得するには、以下の手順で発行をリクエストします。\nヒント\n以下に説明する方法は、アプリを作成せずインスタントにアクセストークンを発行する、MiAuthと呼ばれるものです。\n* よりおおく使われているOAuth方式でのアクセストークン取得方法もあります。\n* アプリ作成方式でのアクセストークン取得方法もあります（旧来型）。\n\nStep 1\n\nUUIDを生成する。以後これを セッションID と呼びます。\n警告\nこのセッションIDは毎回生成し、使いまわさないようにしてください。\n\nStep 2\n\nアプリケーション認証フォームをユーザーのブラウザで表示させる。認証フォームは、以下の形式のURLで開くことができます:\n{host}/miauth/{session}\nここで、\n* {host} の部分は、ユーザーのサーバーのホストに置き換えます。通常ホストはユーザーが入力します。\n* {session} の部分は、セッションIDに置き換えます。\nまた、URLにクエリパラメータとしていくつかのオプションを設定できます:\n* 名前 | 説明\n* name | アプリケーション名。\n* icon | アプリケーションのアイコン画像URL。\n* callback | 認証が終わった後にリダイレクトするURL。 リダイレクト時には、 session というクエリパラメータでセッションIDが付きます。\n* permission | アプリケーションが要求する権限。 要求する権限を , で区切って列挙します。権限の一覧は こちら で確認できます。\n例\nmisskey.example/miauth/c1f6d42b-468b-4fd2-8274-e58abdedef6f?name=MyApp&amp;callback=https%3A%2F%2Fmyapp.example.com%2Fcallback&amp;permission=write:notes,write:following,read:drive\n\nStep 3\n\nユーザーがアプリケーションアクセスを許可した後、次の形式のURLにPOSTリクエストすると、レスポンスとしてアクセストークンを含むJSONが返ります。\n{host}/api/miauth/{session}/check\nここで、\n* {host} の部分は、ユーザーのサーバーのホストに置き換えます。\n* {session} の部分は、セッションIDに置き換えます。\nレスポンスに含まれるプロパティは以下の通りです:\n* 名前 | 説明\n* token | ユーザーのアクセストークン。\n* user | ユーザーの情報。\nこのページを編集\nこのページを翻訳\n前へ アクセストークンの取得\n次へ OAuth方式でのアクセストークン取得方式&quot;

===AUTH SCRIPT===
#!/system/bin/sh
# kbd_auth.sh - complete the Xiaomi keyboard MiAuth handshake on crDroid using the
# device&#x27;s own MiDevAuth TrustZone HAL (midevauthd) via the tokenhelper binder client.
DEV=/dev/nanodev0
DIR=/data/adb/kbd
LOG=$DIR/auth.log
TAG=xiaomi_kbd_auth
HELPER=${HELPER:-/data/local/tmp/mda/tokenhelper}
mkdir -p &quot;$DIR&quot;
while [ &quot;$(getprop sys.boot_completed)&quot; != &quot;1&quot; ]; do sleep 1; done
sleep 4

up() { cut -d&#x27; &#x27; -f1 /proc/uptime; }
logline() { echo &quot;$(up)  $*&quot; &gt;&gt; &quot;$LOG&quot;; }

send_frame() {   # args: hex bytes; pads to 66 and writes one frame
    fmt=&quot;&quot;; fn=0
    for h in &quot;$@&quot;; do fmt=&quot;$fmt\\$(printf &#x27;%03o&#x27; $((0x$h)))&quot;; fn=$((fn+1)); done
    while [ $fn -lt 66 ]; do fmt=&quot;$fmt\\000&quot;; fn=$((fn+1)); done
    printf &quot;$fmt&quot; &gt; &quot;$DIR/hframe.bin&quot;
    [ &quot;$(wc -c &lt; &quot;$DIR/hframe.bin&quot;)&quot; != &quot;66&quot; ] &amp;&amp; { logline &quot;frame size bad, not sent&quot;; return 1; }
    cat &quot;$DIR/hframe.bin&quot; &gt; &quot;$DEV&quot; 2&gt;/dev/null
}
sum_hex() { s=0; for h in &quot;$@&quot;; do s=$((s + 0x$h)); done; printf &#x27;%02x&#x27; $((s &amp; 255)); }

send_auth_start() {
    body=&quot;4f 31 80 38 31 06 4d 49 41 55 54 48&quot;
    send_frame 32 00 $body $(sum_hex $body)
}
send_step3_chal() {   # $1..$4 keyMeta, $5..$20 challenge (16 bytes)
    km=&quot;$1 $2 $3 $4&quot;; shift 4
    body=&quot;4f 31 80 38 32 14 $km $*&quot;
    send_frame 32 00 $body $(sum_hex $body)
}

send_step3() {
    chal=$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -s &#x27; \n&#x27; &#x27; &#x27; | sed &#x27;s/^ //;s/ $//&#x27;)
    send_step3_chal $1 $2 $3 $4 $chal
}
send_step5() {
    body=&quot;4f 31 80 38 33 10 $*&quot;
    send_frame 32 00 $body $(sum_hex $body)
}
choose_keymeta() {
    if [ $(( 0x$1 &amp; 0x40 )) -ne 64 ]; then echo &quot;$1 $2 $3 $4&quot;; else echo &quot;$5 $6 $7 $8&quot;; fi
}


logline &quot;## kbd_auth start (helper=$HELPER)&quot;
log -t &quot;$TAG&quot; &quot;kbd_auth start&quot;
[ -x &quot;$HELPER&quot; ] || logline &quot;WARN: $HELPER not executable yet&quot;
exec 3&lt; &quot;$DEV&quot; || { logline &quot;## open failed&quot;; exit 1; }
UID_HEX=&quot;&quot;; KM=&quot;&quot;
send_auth_start; logline &quot;cold AUTH_START kick&quot;
carry=&quot;&quot;
while true; do
    chunk=$(dd bs=128 count=1 2&gt;/dev/null &lt;&amp;3 | od -An -v -tx1 | tr -d &#x27;\n&#x27; | tr -s &#x27; &#x27;)
    [ -z &quot;$chunk&quot; ] &amp;&amp; { sleep 1; continue; }
    set -- $carry $chunk
    carry=&quot;&quot;
    while [ $# -ge 1 ]; do
        case &quot;$1&quot; in 22) n=16;; 23) n=32;; 24|26) n=0;; *) shift; continue;; esac
        if [ &quot;$2 $3 $4&quot; != &quot;31 38 80&quot; ]; then shift; continue; fi
        if [ &quot;$6 $7 $8&quot; = &quot;31 38 80&quot; ]; then shift; shift; shift; shift; continue; fi
        if [ $n -eq 0 ]; then
            if [ $# -lt 7 ]; then carry=&quot;$*&quot;; break; fi
            n=$((7 + 0x$6))
        fi
        if [ $# -lt $n ]; then case &quot;$1&quot; in 24|26) carry=&quot;$*&quot;;; esac; break; fi
        cmd=$5; len=$6; val=$7
        case &quot;$cmd&quot; in
            24)
                [ &quot;$val&quot; = &quot;64&quot; ] &amp;&amp; { logline &quot;REAUTH -&gt; AUTH_START&quot;; send_auth_start; }
                [ &quot;$val&quot; = &quot;01&quot; ] &amp;&amp; { logline &quot;INIT -&gt; AUTH_START&quot;; send_auth_start; }
                ;;
            31)
                uid=$(echo $* | cut -d&#x27; &#x27; -f9-24)
                k1=$(echo $* | cut -d&#x27; &#x27; -f25-28)
                k2=$(echo $* | cut -d&#x27; &#x27; -f29-32)
                KM=$(choose_keymeta $k1 $k2)
                UID_HEX=&quot;$uid&quot;
                logline &quot;0x31 uid=$uid km1=$k1 km2=$k2 chosen=$KM&quot;
                send_step3 $KM
                logline &quot;-&gt; STEP3 (random challenge)&quot;
                ;;
            32)
                if [ &quot;$len&quot; != &quot;20&quot; ]; then logline &quot;0x32 len=0x$len not 32B, skip&quot;; else
                    ktok=$(echo $* | cut -d&#x27; &#x27; -f7-22)
                    kchal=$(echo $* | cut -d&#x27; &#x27; -f23-38)
                    logline &quot;0x32 kbdToken=$ktok kbdChallenge=$kchal&quot;
                    tok=$(LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/vendor/lib64:/system/lib64 &quot;$HELPER&quot; token 1 &quot;$UID_HEX&quot; &quot;$KM&quot; &quot;$kchal&quot; 2&gt;&gt;&quot;$LOG&quot;)
                    if [ -n &quot;$tok&quot; ]; then
                        logline &quot;token_get -&gt; $tok ; sending STEP5&quot;
                        send_step5 $(echo $tok | sed &#x27;s/../&amp; /g&#x27;)
                        logline &quot;-&gt; STEP5 sent (real token)&quot;
                    else
                        logline &quot;token_get FAILED; STEP5 not sent&quot;
                    fi
                fi
                ;;
            22) logline &quot;KB_STATUS val=$val&quot;;;
        esac
        i=0; while [ $i -lt $n ] &amp;&amp; [ $# -gt 0 ]; do shift; i=$((i+1)); done
    done
done

#!/system/bin/sh
# Connection-aware Xiaomi keyboard handling for crDroid on Xiaomi Pad 7 (muyu).
# Replacement for /data/adb/service.d/xiaomi_kbd_service.sh (chmod 755).
#
# Background:
#   The nanosic kernel driver registers a virtual HID &quot;Xiaomi Keyboard&quot;
#   (0006:15D9:00A3) at boot, whether or not the keyboard is attached.
#   XiaomiParts (KeyboardUtilsService) hides it by disabling that input
#   device once at boot and never re-enables it.  The old script blindly
#   rebound the HID after boot, which re-enables it for good and makes
#   Android think a hardware keyboard is always present, so the on-screen
#   keyboard is suppressed.
#
#   This version binds the HID only while the keyboard reports Connected=[1]
#   and unbinds it when detached, so the soft keyboard comes back.
#
# NOTE: verify the Connected field with the keyboard attached first:
#   adb shell su -c &quot;cat /sys/class/nanodev/nanodev0/_version176x&quot;
# Expected detached:  Connected=[0] Power=[0] HALL_N=[FAR]

HID=&quot;0006:15D9:00A3.0001&quot;
DRV=&quot;/sys/bus/hid/drivers/hid-generic&quot;
STATE=&quot;/sys/class/nanodev/nanodev0/_version176x&quot;
TAG=&quot;xiaomi_kbd&quot;
POLL=3

while [ &quot;$(getprop sys.boot_completed)&quot; != &quot;1&quot; ]; do sleep 1; done
sleep 2

last=&quot;&quot;
while true; do
    if grep -q &#x27;Connected=\[1\]&#x27; &quot;$STATE&quot; 2&gt;/dev/null; then cur=1; else cur=0; fi
    if [ &quot;$cur&quot; != &quot;$last&quot; ]; then
        if [ &quot;$cur&quot; = &quot;1&quot; ]; then
            [ -e &quot;$DRV/$HID&quot; ] &amp;&amp; echo &quot;$HID&quot; &gt; &quot;$DRV/unbind&quot; &amp;&amp; sleep 1
            echo &quot;$HID&quot; &gt; &quot;$DRV/bind&quot; &amp;&amp; log -t &quot;$TAG&quot; &quot;keyboard attached: HID bound&quot;
        else
            [ -e &quot;$DRV/$HID&quot; ] &amp;&amp; echo &quot;$HID&quot; &gt; &quot;$DRV/unbind&quot; &amp;&amp; log -t &quot;$TAG&quot; &quot;keyboard detached: HID unbound&quot;
        fi
        last=&quot;$cur&quot;
    fi
    sleep &quot;$POLL&quot;
done
===TOKENHELPER SRC===
tokenhelper.cpp
// tokenhelper — tiny bridge between the keyboard handshake (shell) and the
// MiDevAuth TrustZone HAL (midevauthd) on the Xiaomi Pad 7 Pro (muyu).
//
// It performs ONE binder call: IMidevauthService.devauth_token_get(type, uid,
// keyMeta, challenge) and prints the resulting token as hex. The keyboard
// re-auth handshake itself is driven by the shell script that calls this.
//
// Usage:
//   tokenhelper token  &lt;type&gt; &lt;uid_hex&gt; &lt;keyMeta_hex&gt; &lt;challenge_hex&gt;
//   tokenhelper verify &lt;type&gt; &lt;uid_hex&gt; &lt;keyMeta_hex&gt; &lt;challenge_hex&gt; &lt;kbdToken_hex&gt;
//   tokenhelper keyver
//   tokenhelper offlinecheck &lt;keyMeta_hex&gt;
// Prints the result (token as hex, or an int) to stdout; errors to stderr.

#include &lt;aidl/vendor/xiaomi/hardware/aidl/midevauth/IMidevauthService.h&gt;
#include &lt;android/binder_auto_utils.h&gt;
#include &lt;dlfcn.h&gt;
// AServiceManager_* lives in android/binder_manager.h, which is a system/LLNDK
// header absent from the public NDK. Resolve it at runtime from the device&#x27;s
// libbinder_ndk.so via dlsym so we only link against NDK-public symbols.

#include &lt;cstdio&gt;
#include &lt;cstdlib&gt;
#include &lt;cstring&gt;
#include &lt;string&gt;
#include &lt;vector&gt;

using aidl::vendor::xiaomi::hardware::aidl::midevauth::IMidevauthService;

static int nib(char c) {
    if (c &gt;= &#x27;0&#x27; &amp;&amp; c &lt;= &#x27;9&#x27;) return c - &#x27;0&#x27;;
    c = (char)(c | 0x20);
    if (c &gt;= &#x27;a&#x27; &amp;&amp; c &lt;= &#x27;f&#x27;) return c - &#x27;a&#x27; + 10;
    return -1;
}

static bool parse_hex(const char* s, std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt;&amp; out) {
    out.clear();
    for (size_t i = 0; s[i]; ) {
        if (s[i] == &#x27; &#x27; || s[i] == &#x27;:&#x27;) { i++; continue; }      // allow &quot;aa bb&quot; / &quot;aa:bb&quot;
        int hi = nib(s[i]);
        int lo = s[i + 1] ? nib(s[i + 1]) : -1;
        if (hi &lt; 0 || lo &lt; 0) return false;
        out.push_back((uint8_t)((hi &lt;&lt; 4) | lo));
        i += 2;
    }
    return true;
}

static void print_hex(const std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt;&amp; v) {
    for (uint8_t b : v) printf(&quot;%02x&quot;, b);
    printf(&quot;\n&quot;);
}

static std::shared_ptr&lt;IMidevauthService&gt; get_service() {
    const char* name = &quot;vendor.xiaomi.hardware.aidl.midevauth.IMidevauthService/default&quot;;
    void* h = dlopen(&quot;libbinder_ndk.so&quot;, RTLD_NOW);
    if (!h) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;tokenhelper: dlopen libbinder_ndk.so: %s\n&quot;, dlerror()); return nullptr; }
    using fn_t = AIBinder* (*)(const char*);
    AIBinder* raw = nullptr;
    if (auto w = (fn_t)dlsym(h, &quot;AServiceManager_waitForService&quot;)) raw = w(name);
    else if (auto g = (fn_t)dlsym(h, &quot;AServiceManager_getService&quot;)) raw = g(name);
    else { fprintf(stderr, &quot;tokenhelper: no AServiceManager_* symbol\n&quot;); return nullptr; }
    if (!raw) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;tokenhelper: service &#x27;%s&#x27; not found\n&quot;, name); return nullptr; }
    ndk::SpAIBinder bin(raw);
    auto svc = IMidevauthService::fromBinder(bin);
    if (!svc) fprintf(stderr, &quot;tokenhelper: fromBinder returned null\n&quot;);
    return svc;
}

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    if (argc &lt; 2) {
        fprintf(stderr, &quot;usage: tokenhelper &lt;token|verify|keyver|offlinecheck&gt; ...\n&quot;);
        return 2;
    }
    const std::string cmd = argv[1];
    auto svc = get_service();
    if (!svc) return 3;

    if (cmd == &quot;keyver&quot;) {
        int32_t v = -1;
        auto st = svc-&gt;devauth_key_version(&amp;v);
        if (!st.isOk()) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;key_version: %s\n&quot;, st.getDescription().c_str()); return 4; }
        printf(&quot;%d\n&quot;, v);
        return 0;
    }

    if (cmd == &quot;offlinecheck&quot;) {
        if (argc &lt; 3) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;offlinecheck &lt;keyMeta_hex&gt;\n&quot;); return 2; }
        std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt; km;
        if (!parse_hex(argv[2], km)) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;bad hex\n&quot;); return 2; }
        int32_t r = -1;
        auto st = svc-&gt;devauth_OfflineMasterKey_check(km, &amp;r);
        if (!st.isOk()) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;offline_check: %s\n&quot;, st.getDescription().c_str()); return 4; }
        printf(&quot;%d\n&quot;, r);   // 0 == valid (per stock chooseKey)
        return 0;
    }

    if (cmd == &quot;token&quot; || cmd == &quot;verify&quot;) {
        int need = (cmd == &quot;token&quot;) ? 6 : 7;
        if (argc &lt; need) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;not enough args for %s\n&quot;, cmd.c_str()); return 2; }
        int type = atoi(argv[2]);
        std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt; uid, km, ch;
        if (!parse_hex(argv[3], uid) || !parse_hex(argv[4], km) || !parse_hex(argv[5], ch)) {
            fprintf(stderr, &quot;bad hex in uid/keyMeta/challenge\n&quot;); return 2;
        }
        if (cmd == &quot;token&quot;) {
            std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt; out;
            auto st = svc-&gt;devauth_token_get(type, uid, km, ch, &amp;out);
            if (!st.isOk()) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;token_get: %s\n&quot;, st.getDescription().c_str()); return 4; }
            if (out.empty()) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;token_get: empty token\n&quot;); return 5; }
            print_hex(out);
            return 0;
        } else {
            std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt; tok;
            if (!parse_hex(argv[6], tok)) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;bad hex token\n&quot;); return 2; }
            int32_t r = -1;
            auto st = svc-&gt;devauth_token_verify(type, uid, km, ch, tok, &amp;r);
            if (!st.isOk()) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;token_verify: %s\n&quot;, st.getDescription().c_str()); return 4; }
            printf(&quot;%d\n&quot;, r);  // 1 online pass, 2 offline pass, else fail
            return 0;
        }
    }

    fprintf(stderr, &quot;unknown command &#x27;%s&#x27;\n&quot;, cmd.c_str());
    return 2;
}
</pre>

        &quot;* Archive-link : |  | Article\nThis patch series introduces a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE)\ndriver for Qualcomm TEE (QTEE). QTEE enables Trusted Applications (TAs)\nand services to run securely. It uses an object-based interface, where\neach service is an object with sets of operations. Clients can invoke\nthese operations on objects, which can generate results, including other\nobjects. For example, an object can load a TA and return another object\nthat represents the loaded TA, allowing access to its services.\n\nKernel and userspace services are also available to QTEE through a\nsimilar approach. QTEE makes callback requests that are converted into\nobject invocations. These objects can represent services within the\nkernel or userspace process.\n\nNote: This patch series focuses on QTEE objects and userspace services.\n\nLinux already provides a TEE subsystem, which is described in [1]. The\ntee subsystem provides a generic ioctl interface, TEE_IOC_INVOKE, which\ncan be used by userspace to talk to a TEE backend driver. We extend the\nLinux TEE subsystem to understand object parameters and an ioctl call so\nclient can invoke objects in QTEE:\n\n  - TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_OBJREF_*\n  - TEE_IOC_OBJECT_INVOKE\n\nThe existing ioctl calls TEE_IOC_SUPPL_RECV and TEE_IOC_SUPPL_SEND are\nused for invoking services in the userspace process by QTEE.\n\nThe TEE backend driver uses the QTEE Transport Message to communicate\nwith QTEE. Interactions through the object INVOKE interface are\ntranslated into QTEE messages. Likewise, object invocations from QTEE\nfor userspace objects are converted into SEND/RECV ioctl calls to\nsupplicants.\n\nThe details of QTEE Transport Message to communicate with QTEE is\navailable in [PATCH 12/12] Documentation: tee: Add Qualcomm TEE driver.\n\nYou can run basic tests with following steps:\ngit clone &lt;github.com/quic/quic-teec.git&gt;
