QTEE enables Trusted Applications (TAs)\nand services to run securely. It uses an object-based interface, where\neach service is an object with sets of operations. Clients can invoke\nthese operations on objects, which can generate results, including other\nobjects. For example, an object can load a TA and return another object\nthat represents the loaded TA, allowing access to its services.\n\nKernel and userspace services are also available to QTEE through a\nsimilar approach. QTEE makes callback requests that are converted into\nobject invocations. These objects can represent services within the\nkernel or userspace process.\n\nNote: This patch series focuses on QTEE objects and userspace services.\n\nLinux already provides a TEE subsystem, which is described in [1]. The\ntee subsystem provides a generic ioctl interface, TEE_IOC_INVOKE, which\ncan be used by userspace to talk to a TEE backend driver. We extend the\nLinux TEE subsystem to understand object parameters and an ioctl call so\nclient can invoke objects in QTEE:\n\n  - TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_OBJREF_*\n  - TEE_IOC_OBJECT_INVOKE\n\nThe existing ioctl calls TEE_IOC_SUPPL_RECV and TEE_IOC_SUPPL_SEND are\nused for invoking services in the userspace process by QTEE.\n\nThe TEE backend driver uses the QTEE Transport Message to communicate\nwith QTEE. Interactions through the object INVOKE interface are\ntranslated into QTEE messages. Likewise, object invocations from QTEE\nfor userspace objects are converted into SEND/RECV ioctl calls to\nsupplicants.\n\nThe details of QTEE Transport Message to communicate with QTEE is\navailable in [PATCH 10/10] Documentation: tee: Add Qualcomm TEE driver.\n\nThis patch series has been tested for basic QTEE object invocations and\ncallback requests, including loading a TA and requesting services form\nthe TA. However, the test platform is currently being prepared for\nupstream availability and will soon be accessible to the community for\nfurther validation. I will share updates as the platform become\navailable.&quot;

        &quot;[PATCH v8 06/11] firmware: qcom: scm: add support for object invocation\n\nAmirreza Zarrabi\n21 Aug 2025 21 Aug &#x27;25\n12:38 a.m.\nQualcomm TEE (QTEE) hosts Trusted Applications (TAs) and services in the secure world, accessed via objects. A QTEE client can invoke these objects to request services. Similarly, QTEE can request services from the nonsecure world using objects exported to the secure world.\n\n...\n\n* drivers/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm.c | 134 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++\n* drivers/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm.h | 7 ++\n* include/linux/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm.h | 6 ++\n* 3 files changed, 147 insertions(+)\ndiff --git a/drivers/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm.c b/drivers/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm.c index edeae6cdcf31..65142fd31118 100644 --- a/drivers/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm.c +++ b/drivers/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm.c @@ -2094,6 +2094,130 @@ static int qcom_scm_qseecom_init(struct qcom_scm *scm)\n#endif /* CONFIG_QCOM_QSEECOM */\n+/** + * qcom_scm_qtee_invoke_smc() - Invoke a QTEE object.\n\n...\n\nqcom_scm_qtee_init(struct qcom_scm *scm) +{ + struct platform_device *qtee_dev; + u64 result, response_type; + int ret; + + /* + * Check if QTEE supports smcinvoke: + * This will fail due to invalid buffers, but first, it checks whether + * the call is supported in QTEE syscall handler. + * If not supported, -EIO is returned. + */ + ret = qcom_scm_qtee_invoke_smc(0, 0, 0, 0, &amp;result, &amp;response_type); + if (ret == -EIO) + return -EIO; + + /* Setup QTEE interface device.\n\n...\n\na/include/linux/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm.h b/include/linux/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm.h index 0f667bf1d4d9..a55ca771286b 100644 --- a/include/linux/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm.h +++ b/include/linux/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm.h @@ -175,4 +175,10 @@ static inline int qcom_scm_qseecom_app_send(u32 app_id,\n#endif /* CONFIG_QCOM_QSEECOM */\n+int qcom_scm_qtee_invoke_smc(phys_addr_t inbuf, size_t inbuf_size, + phys_addr_t outbuf, size_t outbuf_size, + u64 *result, u64 *response_type); +int qcom_scm_qtee_callback_response(phys_addr_t buf, size_t buf_size, + u64 *result, u64 *response_type); + #endif\n-- 2.34.1\n0 0\nBack to the thread\nBack to the list\nPowered by HyperKitty version 1.3.5.&quot;

        &quot;* Page: GitHub code file\n* URL: github.com/wrobelda/goodix-fp-spi-linux/blob/master/docs/01-kernel-tee-driver.md\n* Repository: wrobelda/goodix-fp-spi-linux\n* Path: docs/01-kernel-tee-driver.md\n* Ref: master\n* Lines: 483\n\nLayer 1: the kernel TEE driver\n\nThe QSEECOM TEE driver exposes Qualcomm&#x27;s QSEE trusted applications through the standard TEE subsystem. Source: branch qcom-qseecom-tee at wrobelda/linux (drivers/tee/qseecom/, CONFIG_TEE_QSEECOM).\nThe driver is application-agnostic; this document is not entirely. Nothing in the driver knows anything about fingerprints. The devices, the ioctls, the parameter layouts, the load path and the listener mechanism described here are the interface to any QSEE application. None of it changes when the application changes.\nOnly the concrete values plugged into that interface change:\n* a patch offset;\n* a buffer size;\n* a command number.\nThose values belong to gfenu. They appear here as worked examples, because an interface is easier to follow with real numbers in it. A different application drives the same driver in the same way, with its own numbers.\ngfenu is also the only application the driver has been exercised against so far. This is a statement about test coverage, not about what the driver supports.\n\nWhy this driver\n\nLinux already has QSEECOM support in drivers/firmware/qcom/, but only for in-kernel users such as uefisecapp. A userspace process has no way to open a session to a trusted application and invoke commands in it, and no way to answer the file-I/O requests such an application raises while it works.\nWithout both, a fingerprint sensor of this kind does nothing. The sensor only captures images and raises interrupts. Every decision happens inside the trusted application:\n* image processing;\n* template construction;\n* matching.\nThe secure world has no storage of its own, so what the application builds is sealed and handed back to the normal world to keep. Because of this, the application cannot even finish its first initialisation unless something is answering its file I/O.\nWhy not the QTEE driver. The kernel already carries a Qualcomm TEE driver: qcomtee, documented as QTEE. It exposes an interface called smcinvoke, and smcinvoke is the wrong interface for this application. This needs spelling out, because \&quot;Qualcomm already has a TEE driver\&quot; is the first objection anyone raises.\nQualcomm&#x27;s secure world can be reached through two different interfaces. Which one a system needs is decided by the applications in its firmware, not by the age of its SoC. QSEECOM is command-based: load an application by name, send it a numbered command, service the listener requests it raises. smcinvoke, which qcomtee serves, is object-based.\nThey are not two routes to the same thing. A trusted application is built against one interface or the other; one that answers commands over QSEECOM is not reachable as an smcinvoke object. Platforms offering both are common, because smcinvoke has been available for years while applications continued to be built against QSEECOM. So the presence of QTEE says nothing about whether the applications in that platform&#x27;s firmware can be reached through it. The SM8250 this was developed against is such a platform: it exposes both, and gfenu answers only on QSEECOM.\n\n...\n\nDevices\n\n* node | use\n* /dev/tee0 | client: open a session against an application, invoke commands\n* /dev/teepriv0 | privileged: register a listener, or load an application. The two are told apart by the first parameter — a VALUE holding a listener id, or a MEMREF holding an application name\nTEE_IOC_VERSION reports impl_id = 5 (TEE_IMPL_ID_QSEECOM). Note that a device may also expose qcomtee as tee1 with impl_id = 4. As Why this driver explains, that is a different interface and gfenu does not answer on it.\n\nOpening a session&quot;

      &quot;publish_date&quot;: null,
      &quot;excerpts&quot;: [
        &quot;QTEE (Qualcomm Trusted Execution Environment) ¶\n\nThe QTEE driver handles communication with Qualcomm TEE [1].\nThe lowest level of communication with QTEE builds on the ARM SMC Calling Convention (SMCCC) [2], which is the foundation for QTEE’s Secure Channel Manager (SCM) [3] used internally by the driver.\nIn a QTEE-based system, services are represented as objects with a series of operations that can be called to produce results, including other objects.\nWhen an object is hosted within QTEE, executing its operations is referred to as “direct invocation”. QTEE can also invoke objects hosted in the non-secure world using a method known as “callback request”.\n\n...\n\n|   libqcomtee [5]    |  | subsys | driver |             | Trusted OS   |\n+-------+-------------+--+----+-------+----+-------------+--------------+\n|      Generic TEE API        |       |   QTEE MSG                      |\n|      IOCTL (TEE_IOC_*)      |       |   SMCCC (QCOM_SCM_SMCINVOKE_*)  |\n+-----------------------------+       +---------------------------------+\n\nReferences ¶\n\n[1] docs.qualcomm.com/bundle/publicresource/topics/80-70015-11/qualcomm-trusted-execution-environment.html\n[2] infocenter.arm.com/help/topic/com.arm.doc.den0028a/index.html\n[3] drivers/firmware/qcom/qcom_scm.c\n[4] drivers/tee/qcomtee/qcomtee_msg.h\n[5] github.com/quic/quic-teec\n* ©The kernel development community.\n* \n* Powered by Sphinx 5.3.0 &amp; Alabaster 0.7.16 | Page source&quot;

QTEE runs in the Secure World domain on ARM64 CPUs and exposes secure services to Linux running in the Normal World domain.\nThis change enables the QCOMTEE driver as a module to support communication with QTEE.\nQCOMTEE has been tested on a Qualcomm RB3Gen2 board by loading and executing a Trusted Application via tests hosted at github.com/qualcomm/minkipc.\n\nSigned-off-by: Harshal Dev harshal.dev@oss.qualcomm.com\n\nChanges in v4:\n* Updated the commit message as per discussion to clarify the following:\n* Why we are enabling QCOMTEE for all arm64 boards.\n* From which Qualcomm SoC onwards the driver is applicable.\n* What functionality the driver provides.\n* How the functionality has been tested and on which board.\n* Link to v3: lore.kernel.org/r/20251208-qcom_qcomtee_defconfig-v3-1-b50dcf8ab45e@...\nReviewed-by: Sumit Garg sumit.garg@oss.qualcomm.com\n-Sumit\nReviewed-by: Amirreza Zarrabi amirreza.zarrabi@oss.qualcomm.com\n- Amir\n...\n...\nChanges in v3:\n* Updated the commit message to reflect the supported Qualcomm platforms.&quot;

+/*
+ * MiPPS challenge/response from xiaomi-mipps-auth, with Piano&#x27;s stock
+ * command order. The transport and charging policy remain in this driver.
+ */
+static int piano_mca_vdm(struct piano_mca *mca, unsigned int generation,
+			 unsigned int cmd, const u8 *bytes, u32 flag)
+{
+	__le32 payload[MCA_VDM_LEN / 4] = {};
+	unsigned long deadline;
+	size_t len = sizeof(payload[0]);
+	__le32 state, vbus;
+	int attempt, i, ret;
+
+	if (bytes) {
+		for (i = 0; i &lt; ARRAY_SIZE(payload); i++)
+			payload[i] = cpu_to_le32(get_unaligned_be32(bytes + 4 * i));
+		len = sizeof(payload);
+	} else {
+		payload[0] = cpu_to_le32(flag);
+	}
+
+	/* Stock batterysecret retries an unanswered command once. */
+	for (attempt = 0; attempt &lt; 2; attempt++) {
+		if (generation != READ_ONCE(mca-&gt;pdr_generation))
+			return -ENODEV;
+		ret = piano_mca_write(mca, MCA_PROP_VDM_BASE + cmd - 1,
+				      payload, len);
+		if (ret)
+			return ret;
+		msleep(cmd == 4 || cmd == 5 ? 500 : 5);
+		deadline = jiffies + msecs_to_jiffies(1000);
+		do {
+			if (generation != READ_ONCE(mca-&gt;pdr_generation))
+				return -ENODEV;
+			ret = piano_mca_read(mca, MCA_PROP_BUS_VOLT, &amp;vbus, sizeof(vbus));
+			if (ret || le32_to_cpu(vbus) &lt; MCA_VBUS_ONLINE_UV)
+				return ret ?: -ENODEV;
+			ret = piano_mca_read(mca, MCA_PROP_UVDM_STATE, &amp;state, sizeof(state));
+			if (ret)
+				return ret;
+			if (le32_to_cpu(state) == cmd)
+				return 0;
+			msleep(20);
+		} while (time_before(jiffies, deadline));
+	}
+	return -ETIMEDOUT;
+}
+
+static bool piano_mca_mipps_digest(struct piano_mca *mca,
+				  const struct piano_mipps_key *key,
+				  u8 message[20], const u8 response[MCA_VDM_LEN],
+				  u8 digest[SHA256_DIGEST_SIZE], u32 *adapter_id,
+				  unsigned int generation)
+{
+	struct hmac_sha256_key prepared;
+	u32 id;
+	bool matched = false;
+
+	hmac_sha256_preparekey(&amp;prepared, key-&gt;key, sizeof(key-&gt;key));
+	put_unaligned_be32(*adapter_id, message + MCA_VDM_LEN);
+	hmac_sha256(&amp;prepared, message, 20, digest);
+	if (*adapter_id &amp;&amp; !memcmp(response, digest, MCA_VDM_LEN)) {
+		matched = true;
+		goto out;
+	}
+
+	/*
+	 * Firmware can omit or retain an old ID. Recover it only from a valid
+	 * answer to our fresh random challenge, never from a cached identity.
+	 * Limit work to 65536 guesses; reported 32-bit IDs are checked above.
+	 * No match simply leaves this source on ordinary PD/PPS.
+	 */
+	for (id = 0; id &lt; 65536; id++) {
+		if (!(id &amp; 255)) {
+			if (generation != READ_ONCE(mca-&gt;pdr_generation))
+				break;
+			cond_resched();
+		}
+		put_unaligned_be32(id, message + MCA_VDM_LEN);
+		hmac_sha256(&amp;prepared, message, 20, digest);
+		if (!memcmp(response, digest, MCA_VDM_LEN)) {
+			*adapter_id = id;
+			matched = true;
+			break;
+		}
+	}
+ out:
+	memzero_explicit(&amp;prepared, sizeof(prepared));
+	return matched;
+}

<pre>From 7b2c4d08da38b128641a62d5783e73ab349d7b5f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: slwyts &lt;slwyts@foxmail.com&gt;
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 18:25:53 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] HID: nanosic: describe unsupported reports and release full
 touch frames

The vendor MCU adapter does not implement a HID feature/output report
transport. Returning success leaves the allocated feature buffer empty,
so hid-multitouch reports mismatched report IDs during every probe.
Mark the touchpad as having no initial feature queries and reject raw
requests that have no transport. Keep the descriptor-provided limits.

Use the actual variant report size when releasing contacts: Piano uses
27 bytes, while the other supported layout uses 21. Sending a short
frame can leave the tail contact/count fields unprocessed at lid close.
Set the no-query flag in the low-level start callback, after HID core resets
quirks and before hidinput performs its feature mappings.
---
 drivers/hid/hid-nanosic-wn8030.c | 11 ++++++++---
 1 file changed, 8 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/drivers/hid/hid-nanosic-wn8030.c b/drivers/hid/hid-nanosic-wn8030.c
index 0b25473de75..ff14a782555 100644
--- a/drivers/hid/hid-nanosic-wn8030.c
+++ b/drivers/hid/hid-nanosic-wn8030.c
@@ -613,6 +613,10 @@ static int nanosic_wn8030_hid_parse(struct hid_device *hid)
 
 static int nanosic_wn8030_hid_start(struct hid_device *hid)
 {
+	/* HID core resets quirks before probe; set this before input mapping. */
+	if (hid-&gt;product == 0x00A1)
+		hid-&gt;quirks |= HID_QUIRK_NO_INIT_REPORTS;
+
 	return 0;
 }
 
@@ -635,7 +639,8 @@ static int nanosic_wn8030_raw_request(struct hid_device *hid,
 				      __u8 *buf, size_t len,
 				      unsigned char rtype, int reqtype)
 {
-	return len;
+	/* The MCU protocol has no HID feature/output report transport. */
+	return -EOPNOTSUPP;
 }
 
 static inline u32 nanosic_wn8030_checksum32(const u8 *data, int size)
@@ -1501,7 +1506,7 @@ static void nanosic_wn8030_release_inputs(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
 {
 	u8 keyboard[9] = { 0x05 };
 	u8 consumer[3] = { 0x06 };
-	u8 touchpad[21] = { 0x19 };
+	u8 touchpad[27] = { 0x19 };
 
 	if (nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard) {
 		hid_input_report(nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard, HID_INPUT_REPORT,
@@ -1511,7 +1516,7 @@ static void nanosic_wn8030_release_inputs(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
 	}
 	if (nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad)
 		hid_input_report(nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad, HID_INPUT_REPORT,
-				 touchpad, sizeof(touchpad), 0);
+				 touchpad, nanosic-&gt;variant-&gt;touchpad_len, 0);

===README===
# Piano keyboard integration

The kernel owns the WN8030 transport, firmware download, HID keyboard and
consumer keys, LED class controls, attachment switch and power callbacks.
This accessory has no touchpad: its DT sets `nanosic,no-touchpad` and the driver
never creates a touchpad HID device. `SW_TABLET_MODE` is the inverse of the
MCU&#x27;s connected bit; it is independent of the folio Hall policy.

Use `CONFIG_HID_NANOSIC_WN8030=m`, the complete matching module package and
normal distribution udev/kmod OF modalias loading. No keyboard startup service,
module blacklist, manual GPIO/supply setup or dependency on a display/touch
service is needed. GENI/GPI and regulator dependencies are represented in DT
and handled by driver probe/deferred probe. A service becoming active would
not establish keyboard functionality.

The device requests `nanosic/piano/MCU_Upgrade.bin` via `firmware-name`.
`firmware/piano-input.json`, consumed by `tools/firmware_payload.py`, pins the
83,436-byte OS3.0.303.0.WPYCNXM stock extraction to SHA-256
`c03d6b650cb85a983359c6686d831875df10ee1206fd31afc1403baefeb7e407`.
The existing `piano-local-firmware` package already installs these bytes.
No community firmware download, duplicate blob or global alias is required.

Standard interfaces:

- Keyboard/consumer events: evdev through HID; Caps Lock uses HID output.
- Attach/detach: `Xiaomi Keyboard Tablet Mode`, `EV_SW/SW_TABLET_MODE`.
- Backlight: `/sys/class/leds/nanosic::kbd_backlight/brightness` (0–100).
- Mic mute LED: `/sys/class/leds/nanosic::micmute/brightness` (0–1).
- Community `nanosic_hinge`/`nanosic_auth` interfaces are retained, with no
  optional angle/authentication daemon enabled by this integration.

Driver source presence and offline tests do not validate physical LEDs,
reconnection, suspend, wake or energy use. Keep system suspend disabled until
its independent display and platform prerequisites are met.

## Provenance and reuse decision

Kernel: `blu-sharky/linux-piano`, commit
`f8afe7ff7127f46f5339fdaf5c24ecbffbfbb92b`, #17, GPL-2.0-only,
`drivers/hid/hid-nanosic-wn8030.c`, binding and `nanosic_hinge.h`.
The imported commit retains bluseliu50&#x27;s authorship and the original
map220v/ianchb credits and Signed-off-by trailers. The local integration
keeps the board&#x27;s own electrical settings and checked firmware/parser core.

Userspace reviewed (not copied): `blu-sharky/debian-piano`, commit
`a75f8c5d5fa099d65c171ac839c2e3bb6c63ec45`,
`boot/dtbo-piano-keyboard.dts`, `rootfs/overlay/usr/lib/piano/keyboard-start`,
`rootfs/overlay/usr/lib/systemd/system/piano-keyboard.service`,
`rootfs/overlay/etc/modprobe.d/piano.conf` and its `80-drivers.rules`.
Their service explicitly loads the module because their image suppresses OF
module autoload. Piano&#x27;s Ubuntu integration retains standard autoload, so that
workaround and its waits/ordering are unnecessary here. The overlay is wiring
reference only; it is not shipped or applied. This README is included in the
existing desktop package as integration documentation; it adds no service.
</pre>

#!/bin/sh
# keyboard-start: keyboard-cover bring-up (piano-keyboard service).
#
# Runs after piano-touch, which loads the QUP1 GPI DMA controller that the
# keyboard I2C bus (QUP1 SE6) shares with the touchscreen SPI, and after
# piano-display, which loads the GENI I2C driver. Nothing autoloads the
# keyboard driver (of: modaliases are skipped by 80-drivers.rules).
#
# On probe the driver powers the MCU (L11B 1.8 V first, then L14B 3.3 V),
# downloads nanosic/MCU_Upgrade.bin into its RAM and registers the
# keyboard and touchpad HID devices once the cover reports itself.
# /etc/piano/keyboard.conf may set KEYBOARD_START=0 to skip everything.
set -eu

KEYBOARD_START=1
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
[ ! -r /etc/piano/keyboard.conf ] || . /etc/piano/keyboard.conf

BUS=/sys/bus/platform/devices/a98000.i2c

say() {
    echo &quot;piano-keyboard: $*&quot;
    echo &quot;piano-keyboard: $*&quot; &gt; /dev/kmsg 2&gt;/dev/null || true
}

die() {
    say &quot;FAIL: $*&quot;
    exit 1
}

[ &quot;$KEYBOARD_START&quot; = 1 ] || { say &quot;disabled by /etc/piano/keyboard.conf&quot;; exit 0; }

n=0
until [ -e &quot;$BUS/driver&quot; ]; do
    [ &quot;$n&quot; -lt 100 ] || die &#x27;SE6 I2C bus not bound (GPI or GENI I2C missing?)&#x27;
    sleep 0.1; n=$((n + 1))
done

modprobe hid_nanosic_wn8030

n=0
until CLIENT=$(ls -d &quot;$BUS&quot;/i2c-*/*-004c 2&gt;/dev/null) &amp;&amp; [ -e &quot;$CLIENT/driver&quot; ]; do
    [ &quot;$n&quot; -lt 100 ] || die &#x27;keyboard MCU not bound&#x27;
    sleep 0.1; n=$((n + 1))
done
say &quot;DONE $(cat /sys/class/input/input*/name 2&gt;/dev/null | grep -i xiaomi | tr &#x27;\n&#x27; &#x27; &#x27;)&quot;
===SERVICE===
[Unit]
Description=Piano keyboard cover (Nanosic WN8030 keyboard and touchpad)
# piano-touch loads the QUP1 GPI controller, piano-display the GENI I2C driver
After=piano-touch.service piano-display.service
Wants=piano-touch.service
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/lib/piano/keyboard-start
RemainAfterExit=yes
TimeoutStartSec=60
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
===DTBO===
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only
/* Keyboard profile: the keyboard cover behind the pogo pins.
 *
 * A Nanosic WN8030 MCU at 0x4c on QUP1 SE6 bridges the cover&#x27;s keyboard
 * and touchpad.  It boots from RAM: its bootloader takes the stock
 * MCU_Upgrade.bin over I2C at every power-up.  The stock dtbo fragment for
 * the same node stays in place; everything the mainline driver reads is
 * re-stated below.
 *
 *   - dvdd, 3.3 V: stock L14B, which feeds nothing but this MCU and is off
 *     until HLOS enables it (no proxy vote).  The stock kernel votes
 *     3300 mV; the mainline LDO step rounds that up to 3304 mV, and AOP
 *     resets the SoC as soon as that vote is enabled.  3296 mV, the step
 *     below, is safe.
 *   - vddio, 1.8 V: stock L11B, which also feeds the panel and the I2C
 *     pull-ups and is left on by the bootloader.  Declared always-on so no
 *     consumer can ever switch it off; the driver enables it before L14B,
 *     because the MCU must never see 3.3 V without its I/O rail.
 *   - Both are the only regulators of a mainline PM8550 block.
 *   - The SE runs at 1 MHz, as on stock, on GPI DMA (the QUP1 GPI streams
 *     are already matched for the touchscreen SPI).
 *   - Pins as in the stock nanosic_keyboard_mcu / mi_qupv3_se6_i2c states.
 *
 * Nothing loads the keyboard driver on coldplug (of: modaliases are not
 * autoloaded); the piano-keyboard service does, after the touchscreen
 * service has brought up the QUP1 GPI controller.
 */
#include &quot;dtbo-piano-video.dts&quot;
#include &lt;dt-bindings/clock/qcom,sm8750-gcc.h&gt;
#include &lt;dt-bindings/dma/qcom-gpi.h&gt;
#include &lt;dt-bindings/gpio/gpio.h&gt;
#include &lt;dt-bindings/interconnect/qcom,icc.h&gt;
#include &lt;dt-bindings/interconnect/qcom,sm8750-rpmh.h&gt;
#include &lt;dt-bindings/interrupt-controller/irq.h&gt;
#include &lt;dt-bindings/regulator/qcom,rpmh-regulator.h&gt;

/ {
	fragment@320 {
		target = &lt;&amp;apps_rsc&gt;;
		__overlay__ {
			kbd_regs_b: regulators-4 {
				compatible = &quot;qcom,pm8550-rpmh-regulators&quot;;
				qcom,pmic-id = &quot;b&quot;;

				vreg_l11b_1p8_ml: ldo11 {
					regulator-name = &quot;vreg_l11b_1p8_ml&quot;;
					regulator-min-microvolt = &lt;1800000&gt;;
					regulator-max-microvolt = &lt;1800000&gt;;
					regulator-initial-mode = &lt;RPMH_REGULATOR_MODE_HPM&gt;;
					regulator-always-on;
					regulator-boot-on;
				};

				vreg_l14b_3p3_ml: ldo14 {
					regulator-name = &quot;vreg_l14b_3p3_ml&quot;;
					/* never 3304 mV: see above */
					regulator-min-microvolt = &lt;3296000&gt;;
					regulator-max-microvolt = &lt;3296000&gt;;
					regulator-initial-mode = &lt;RPMH_REGULATOR_MODE_HPM&gt;;
				};
			};
		};
	};

	fragment@321 {
		target-path = &quot;/soc&quot;;
		__overlay__ {
			pinctrl@f100000 {
				kbd_i2c6_ml: kbd-i2c6-state {
					pins = &quot;gpio56&quot;, &quot;gpio57&quot;;
					function = &quot;qup1_se6&quot;;
					drive-strength = &lt;2&gt;;
					bias-disable;
				};

				kbd_mcu_ml: kbd-mcu-state {
					sleep-pins {
						pins = &quot;gpio3&quot;;
						function = &quot;gpio&quot;;
						drive-strength = &lt;2&gt;;

# SPDX-License-Identifier: (GPL-2.0-only OR BSD-2-Clause)
%YAML 1.2
---
$id: http://devicetree.org/schemas/input/nanosic,wn8030.yaml#
$schema: http://devicetree.org/meta-schemas/core.yaml#

title: Nanosic WN8030 keyboard cover MCU

maintainers:
  - bluseliu50 &lt;bluseliu50@gmail.com&gt;

description:
  The WN8030 is an I2C-attached microcontroller that bridges a detachable
  keyboard cover (keyboard, touchpad and their LEDs) to the host over pogo
  pins. It boots from RAM, so the host downloads its firmware through the
  MCU bootloader every time the MCU is powered up or reset. The keyboard
  and touchpad are then exposed as HID devices. The board variant selects
  the report descriptors, the command register and the power-up timing.

properties:
  compatible:
    enum:
      - nanosic,wn8030-piano
      - nanosic,wn8030-sheng

  reg:
    maxItems: 1

  interrupts:
    maxItems: 1
    description: Data-ready line, rising edge.

  reset-gpios:
    maxItems: 1

  sleep-gpios:
    maxItems: 1
    description: Keeps the MCU awake while deasserted.

  status-gpios:
    maxItems: 1
    description: Cover attach status reported by the MCU.

  vddio-supply:
    description: 1.8 V I/O and I2C pull-up supply.

  dvdd-supply:
    description: 3.3 V MCU supply. It is switched on only after vddio.

required:
  - compatible
  - reg
  - interrupts
  - reset-gpios
  - sleep-gpios
  - status-gpios
  - vddio-supply
  - dvdd-supply

additionalProperties: false

examples:
  - |
    #include &lt;dt-bindings/gpio/gpio.h&gt;
    #include &lt;dt-bindings/interrupt-controller/irq.h&gt;

    i2c {
        #address-cells = &lt;1&gt;;
        #size-cells = &lt;0&gt;;

        keyboard@4c {
            compatible = &quot;nanosic,wn8030-piano&quot;;
            reg = &lt;0x4c&gt;;
            interrupts-extended = &lt;&amp;tlmm 97 IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_RISING&gt;;
            reset-gpios = &lt;&amp;tlmm 188 GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW&gt;;
            sleep-gpios = &lt;&amp;tlmm 3 GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW&gt;;
            status-gpios = &lt;&amp;tlmm 95 GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH&gt;;
            vddio-supply = &lt;&amp;vreg_l11b_1p8&gt;;
            dvdd-supply = &lt;&amp;vreg_l14b_3p3&gt;;
        };
    };
...

/* Register byte of the bootloader commands */
#define WN8030_BL_REG 0x5c

/**
 * struct nanosic_wn8030_variant - per-device integration of the WN8030
 * @kbd_rdesc: report descriptor of the keyboard HID device
 * @kbd_rsize: size of @kbd_rdesc
 * @tp_rdesc: report descriptor of the touchpad HID device
 * @tp_rsize: size of @tp_rdesc
 * @cmd_reg: register byte that prefixes runtime commands
 * @consumer_len: length of a consumer control report (0x06)
 * @touchpad_len: length of a touchpad report (0x19)
 * @caps_led_mask: LED output report bits that light the Caps Lock LED
 * @packed_reports: a read frame carries several reports back to back
 * @reset_ms: reset pulse after power-up, 0 to leave reset released
 * @boot_ms: wait for the bootrom after reset release
 * @wake_ms: wait after the sleep pin is released
 * @bl_write_ms: wait after every bootloader write
 */
struct nanosic_wn8030_variant {
	const u8 *kbd_rdesc;
	unsigned int kbd_rsize;
	const u8 *tp_rdesc;
	unsigned int tp_rsize;
	u8 cmd_reg;
	u8 consumer_len;
	u8 touchpad_len;
	u8 caps_led_mask;
	bool packed_reports;
	unsigned int reset_ms;
	unsigned int boot_ms;
	unsigned int wake_ms;
	unsigned int bl_write_ms;
};

static const char * const nanosic_wn8030_supply_names[] = {
	&quot;vddio&quot;,	/* I/O power supply (1.8V) */
	&quot;dvdd&quot;,		/* Digital power supply (3.3V) */
};

	struct device *dev;

	struct i2c_client *client;

	struct hid_device *hid_touchpad;

	struct gpio_desc *sleep_gpio;
	struct gpio_desc *reset_gpio;
	struct regulator_bulk_data supplies[ARRAY_SIZE(nanosic_wn8030_supply_names)];

	struct regmap *regmap;
	struct mutex conn_mutex;
	struct delayed_work wake_worker;
	struct work_struct input_state_work;

	bool suspended;
	bool keyboard_attached;
	bool userspace_angle_enabled;
	bool input_enabled;

	bool tablet_mode;
	bool capslock_enabled;
	bool micmute_key_down;

	struct led_classdev kbd_backlight_led;

static int nanosic_wn8030_power_on(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
{
	const struct nanosic_wn8030_variant *variant = nanosic-&gt;variant;
	int ret;

	/*
	 * One at a time, I/O first: regulator_bulk_enable() gives no order,
	 * and the 3.3 V supply must never be up while the 1.8 V I/O supply
	 * is down.
	 */
	ret = regulator_enable(nanosic-&gt;supplies[0].consumer);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to enable %s\n&quot;,
			nanosic-&gt;supplies[0].supply);
		return ret;
	}

	ret = regulator_enable(nanosic-&gt;supplies[1].consumer);
	if (ret) {
		dev_err(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to enable %s\n&quot;,
			nanosic-&gt;supplies[1].supply);
		regulator_disable(nanosic-&gt;supplies[0].consumer);
		return ret;
	}

	if (variant-&gt;reset_ms) {
		gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;reset_gpio, 1);
		msleep(variant-&gt;reset_ms);
	}
	gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;reset_gpio, 0);
	msleep(variant-&gt;boot_ms); /* WN8030 bootrom start */
	gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;sleep_gpio, 0);
	if (variant-&gt;wake_ms)
		msleep(variant-&gt;wake_ms);

	return 0;
}

static void nanosic_wn8030_power_off(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
{
	gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;sleep_gpio, 1);
	gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;reset_gpio, 1);
	msleep(10);
	regulator_disable(nanosic-&gt;supplies[1].consumer);
	regulator_disable(nanosic-&gt;supplies[0].consumer);
}

static void nanosic_wn8030_wake_worker(struct work_struct *data)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic =
		container_of(data, struct nanosic_wn8030, wake_worker.work);

	nanosic_wn8030_set_kb_power(nanosic, true);
	schedule_delayed_work(&amp;nanosic-&gt;wake_worker, msecs_to_jiffies(12000));
}

static void nanosic_wn8030_release_inputs(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
{
	u8 keyboard[9] = { 0x05 };
	u8 consumer[3] = { 0x06 };
	u8 touchpad[21] = { 0x19 };

	if (nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard) {
		hid_input_report(nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard, HID_INPUT_REPORT,
				 keyboard, sizeof(keyboard), 0);
		hid_input_report(nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard, HID_INPUT_REPORT,
				 consumer, sizeof(consumer), 0);
	}
	if (nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad)
		hid_input_report(nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad, HID_INPUT_REPORT,
				 touchpad, sizeof(touchpad), 0);
	WRITE_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;micmute_key_down, false);
}

static void nanosic_wn8030_input_state_work(struct work_struct *work)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic =
		container_of(work, struct nanosic_wn8030, input_state_work);
	bool enable = READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;userspace_angle_enabled) &amp;&amp;
		      !READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;lid_closed) &amp;&amp;
		      !READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;tablet_mode);
	u8 caps_led;
	u8 micmute_led;

	mutex_lock(&amp;nanosic-&gt;conn_mutex);
	caps_led = READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;capslock_enabled) ? 0xFD : 0xFC;
	micmute_led = READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;micmute_led.brightness) ? 0xF7 : 0xF3;
	if (enable != READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;input_enabled)) {
		WRITE_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;input_enabled, enable);
		if (!enable)
			nanosic_wn8030_release_inputs(nanosic);
	}

	if (!nanosic-&gt;keyboard_attached || READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;suspended))
		goto out;

	nanosic_wn8030_set_touchpad(nanosic, enable);
	if (enable) {
		nanosic_wn8030_set_indicator_led(nanosic, caps_led);
		nanosic_wn8030_set_indicator_led(nanosic, micmute_led);
	} else {
		nanosic_wn8030_set_indicator_led(nanosic, 0xFC);
		nanosic_wn8030_set_indicator_led(nanosic, 0xF3);
	}
	nanosic_wn8030_sync_kbd_backlight(nanosic);

out:
	mutex_unlock(&amp;nanosic-&gt;conn_mutex);
}

static void nanosic_wn8030_hall_event(struct input_handle *handle,
				      unsigned int type,
				      unsigned int code, int value)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = handle-&gt;private;

	if (type != EV_SW || (code != SW_LID &amp;&amp; code != SW_TABLET_MODE))
		return;

	if (code == SW_LID)
		WRITE_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;lid_closed, value);
	else
		WRITE_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;tablet_mode, value);
	schedule_work(&amp;nanosic-&gt;input_state_work);
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_hall_connect(struct input_handler *handler,
				       struct input_dev *dev,
				       const struct input_device_id *id)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = handler-&gt;private;
	struct input_handle *handle = &amp;nanosic-&gt;hall_handle;
	int ret;

	if (handle-&gt;dev)
		return -EEXIST;

	handle-&gt;dev = input_get_device(dev);
	handle-&gt;handler = handler;

static int nanosic_wn8030_suspend(struct device *dev)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = dev_get_drvdata(dev);

	WRITE_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;suspended, true);
	disable_irq(nanosic-&gt;client-&gt;irq);
	cancel_delayed_work_sync(&amp;nanosic-&gt;wake_worker);
	cancel_work_sync(&amp;nanosic-&gt;input_state_work);

	gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;sleep_gpio, 1);
	msleep(10);

	return 0;
}

/*
 * Hand one report to its consumer.  @len is what is left of the read frame
 * from @p on; returns the length of the report, or 0 if the frame ends here.
 */
static int nanosic_wn8030_dispatch(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic,
				   const u8 *p, int len)
{
	const struct nanosic_wn8030_variant *variant = nanosic-&gt;variant;
	int size;

	switch (p[0]) {
	case 0x2:
		size = 8;
		break;
	case 0x5:
		size = 9;
		break;
	case 0x6:
		size = variant-&gt;consumer_len;
		break;
	case 0x19:
		size = variant-&gt;touchpad_len;
		break;
	case 0x22:
		size = 16;
		break;
	case 0x23:
		size = 32;
		break;
	case 0x24:
	case 0x26:
		size = len;
		break;
	default:
		return 0;
	}

	if (size &gt; len)
		return 0;

	switch (p[0]) {
	case 0x2:
		if (READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;input_enabled) &amp;&amp; nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard)
			hid_input_report(nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard, HID_INPUT_REPORT,
					 (u8 *)p, size, 0);
		break;
	case 0x5: {
		bool micmute_down;
		bool micmute_was_down;

		if (!READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;input_enabled))
			break;
		micmute_down = nanosic_wn8030_report_has_key(p, 0x6f);
		micmute_was_down = READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;micmute_key_down);
		if (micmute_down &amp;&amp; !micmute_was_down)
			WRITE_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;micmute_key_down, true);
		if (nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard)
			hid_input_report(nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard, HID_INPUT_REPORT,
					 (u8 *)p, size, 0);
		if (!micmute_down &amp;&amp; micmute_was_down) {
			bool enable;

			/* Do not send the LED command before the key release report. */
			mutex_lock(&amp;nanosic-&gt;conn_mutex);
			nanosic-&gt;micmute_key_down = false;
			enable = READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;micmute_led.brightness) != LED_OFF;
			nanosic_wn8030_sync_micmute_led(nanosic, enable);
			mutex_unlock(&amp;nanosic-&gt;conn_mutex);
		}
		break;
	}
	case 0x6:
		if (READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;input_enabled) &amp;&amp; nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard)
			hid_input_report(nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard, HID_INPUT_REPORT,
					 (u8 *)p, size, 0);
		break;
	case 0x19:
		if (READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;input_enabled) &amp;&amp; nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad)
			hid_input_report(nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad, HID_INPUT_REPORT,
					 (u8 *)p, size, 0);
		break;
	default:
		/* A lone report may run on into the rest of the frame. */
		nanosic_wn8030_handle_vendor(nanosic, p,
					     variant-&gt;packed_reports ? size : len);
		break;
	}

	return size;
}

static irqreturn_t nanosic_wn8030_handler(int irq, void *data)
{
	int ret;
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = data;
	u8 buf[XM_WN8030_I2C_READ];
	int len, size, off;

	/* After sleep pin deactivated, fw will trigger irq to notify about
	 * successful resume, second irq will tell about kb connection state
	 */
	if (READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;suspended)) {
		WRITE_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;suspended, false);
		schedule_work(&amp;nanosic-&gt;input_state_work);
		return IRQ_HANDLED;
	}

	ret = regmap_bulk_read(nanosic-&gt;regmap, 0x4c, buf, sizeof(buf));
	if (ret) {
		dev_warn(nanosic-&gt;dev, &quot;failed to read data on irq %d\n&quot;, ret);
		return IRQ_HANDLED;
	}

	/* Bad data */
	if (buf[0] != 0x57 || buf[2] == 0x0)
		return IRQ_HANDLED;

	off = 3;
	do {
		len = sizeof(buf) - off;
		size = nanosic_wn8030_dispatch(nanosic, &amp;buf[off], len);
		off += size;
	} while (nanosic-&gt;variant-&gt;packed_reports &amp;&amp; size &amp;&amp; off &lt; sizeof(buf));

	//print_hex_dump(KERN_INFO, &quot;&quot;, DUMP_PREFIX_OFFSET, 16, 1, buf, sizeof(buf), false);

	return IRQ_HANDLED;
}

{
	int ret;

	ret = regmap_bulk_write(nanosic-&gt;regmap, WN8030_BL_REG, buf, len);
	if (nanosic-&gt;variant-&gt;bl_write_ms)

static ssize_t nanosic_hinge_write(struct file *file, const char __user *buf,
				   size_t count, loff_t *off)
{
	struct nanosic_hinge_file *ctx = file-&gt;private_data;
	struct nanosic_hinge_control control;

	if (count != sizeof(control))
		return -EINVAL;
	if (copy_from_user(&amp;control, buf, sizeof(control)))
		return -EFAULT;
	if (control.version != NANOSIC_HINGE_ABI_VERSION ||
	    control.flags &amp; ~NANOSIC_HINGE_CONTROL_ENABLE)
		return -EINVAL;

	WRITE_ONCE(ctx-&gt;nanosic-&gt;userspace_angle_enabled,
		   control.flags &amp; NANOSIC_HINGE_CONTROL_ENABLE);
	schedule_work(&amp;ctx-&gt;nanosic-&gt;input_state_work);
	return sizeof(control);
}

static __poll_t nanosic_hinge_poll(struct file *file, poll_table *wait)
{
	struct nanosic_hinge_file *ctx = file-&gt;private_data;
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = ctx-&gt;nanosic;

	poll_wait(file, &amp;nanosic-&gt;hinge_read_wq, wait);
	if (READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;hinge_sequence) != ctx-&gt;sequence)
		return EPOLLIN | EPOLLRDNORM;
	return 0;
}

static void nanosic_wn8030_remove(struct i2c_client *client)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = i2c_get_clientdata(client);

	devm_led_classdev_unregister(nanosic-&gt;dev, &amp;nanosic-&gt;kbd_backlight_led);
	devm_led_classdev_unregister(nanosic-&gt;dev, &amp;nanosic-&gt;micmute_led);
	input_unregister_handler(&amp;nanosic-&gt;hall_handler);
	cancel_work_sync(&amp;nanosic-&gt;input_state_work);
	disable_irq(nanosic-&gt;client-&gt;irq);
	cancel_delayed_work_sync(&amp;nanosic-&gt;wake_worker);

	misc_deregister(&amp;nanosic-&gt;hinge_misc);
	misc_deregister(&amp;nanosic-&gt;auth_misc);

	if (nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard)
		hid_destroy_device(nanosic-&gt;hid_keyboard);
	if (nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad)
		hid_destroy_device(nanosic-&gt;hid_touchpad);
	nanosic_wn8030_power_off(nanosic);
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_resume(struct device *dev)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = dev_get_drvdata(dev);

	enable_irq(nanosic-&gt;client-&gt;irq);

	gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;sleep_gpio, 0);
	msleep(25);

	if (READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;suspended)) {
		dev_warn(dev, &quot;timeout waiting for chip resume. Reseting chip...\n&quot;);
		gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;reset_gpio, 1);
		msleep(nanosic-&gt;variant-&gt;reset_ms ?: 10);
		gpiod_set_value_cansleep(nanosic-&gt;reset_gpio, 0);
		msleep(nanosic-&gt;variant-&gt;boot_ms);
		WRITE_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;suspended, false);
		return nanosic_wn8030_load_fw(nanosic);
	}

	/* Wake up keyboard after MCU exits sleep */
	nanosic_wn8030_set_kb_power(nanosic, true);
	schedule_work(&amp;nanosic-&gt;input_state_work);

static int nanosic_wn8030_xm_auth_init(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic)
{
	u8 buf[XM_WN8030_I2C_WRITE] = { 0x32, 0x00, 0x4F, 0x31,
					0x80, 0x38, 0x31, 0x06,
					0x4d, 0x49, 0x41, 0x55, 0x54, 0x48,
					0x00 };

	buf[14] = nanosic_wn8030_checksum8(&amp;buf[2], 13);

	return nanosic_wn8030_cmd(nanosic, buf);
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_xm_auth_s3t1(struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic, u8 *key_meta, u8 *challenge)
{

					0x80, 0x38, 0x32, 0x14,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,

	memcpy(&amp;buf[8], key_meta, 4);
	memcpy(&amp;buf[12], challenge, 16);
	buf[28] = nanosic_wn8030_checksum8(&amp;buf[2], 26);

	return nanosic_wn8030_cmd(nanosic, buf);
}

					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
					0x00 };

	memcpy(&amp;buf[8], token, 16);
	buf[24] = nanosic_wn8030_checksum8(&amp;buf[2], 22);

	return nanosic_wn8030_cmd(nanosic, buf);
}

static int nanosic_wn8030_output_report(struct hid_device *hid, u8 *buf, size_t count)

/ {
	/*
	 * The OEM node uses downstream binding (compatible &quot;qcom,i2c-geni&quot;,
	 * clock named &quot;se-clk&quot;) and only a transmit DMA specifier. The mainline
	 * geni-i2c driver matches &quot;qcom,geni-i2c&quot; and looks up a clock named
	 * &quot;se&quot;, so the controller never probes and no i2c client is created for
	 * the keyboard. Normalize it the same way the other QUP buses are.
	 */
	fragment@250 {
		target = &lt;&amp;qupv3_se3_i2c&gt;;
		__overlay__ {
			compatible = &quot;qcom,geni-i2c&quot;;
			clock-names = &quot;se&quot;;
			clock-frequency = &lt;400000&gt;;
			dmas = &lt;&amp;gpi_dma0 0 3 3&gt;, &lt;&amp;gpi_dma0 1 3 3&gt;;
			status = &quot;okay&quot;;
		};
	};

	fragment@251 {
		target = &lt;&amp;qupv3_se3_i2c&gt;;

static ssize_t nanosic_hinge_write(struct file *file, const char __user *buf,
				   size_t count, loff_t *off)
{
	struct nanosic_hinge_file *ctx = file-&gt;private_data;
	struct nanosic_hinge_control control;

	if (count != sizeof(control))
		return -EINVAL;
	if (copy_from_user(&amp;control, buf, sizeof(control)))
		return -EFAULT;
	if (control.version != NANOSIC_HINGE_ABI_VERSION ||
	    control.flags &amp; ~NANOSIC_HINGE_CONTROL_ENABLE)
		return -EINVAL;

	WRITE_ONCE(ctx-&gt;nanosic-&gt;userspace_angle_enabled,
		   control.flags &amp; NANOSIC_HINGE_CONTROL_ENABLE);
	schedule_work(&amp;ctx-&gt;nanosic-&gt;input_state_work);
	return sizeof(control);
}

static __poll_t nanosic_hinge_poll(struct file *file, poll_table *wait)
{
	struct nanosic_hinge_file *ctx = file-&gt;private_data;
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = ctx-&gt;nanosic;

	poll_wait(file, &amp;nanosic-&gt;hinge_read_wq, wait);
	if (READ_ONCE(nanosic-&gt;hinge_sequence) != ctx-&gt;sequence)
		return EPOLLIN | EPOLLRDNORM;
	return 0;
}

static const struct file_operations nanosic_hinge_fops = {
	.owner = THIS_MODULE,
	.open = nanosic_hinge_open,
	.release = nanosic_hinge_release,
	.read = nanosic_hinge_read,
	.write = nanosic_hinge_write,
	.poll = nanosic_hinge_poll,
	.llseek = noop_llseek,
};

struct nanosic_auth_req {
	u8 uid[16];
	u8 challenge[16];
};

static int nanosic_auth_open(struct inode *inode, struct file *file)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic =
		container_of(file-&gt;private_data, struct nanosic_wn8030, auth_misc);

	if (nanosic-&gt;auth_open)
		return -EBUSY;
	nanosic-&gt;auth_open = true;
	file-&gt;private_data = nanosic;
	return 0;
}

static int nanosic_auth_release(struct inode *inode, struct file *file)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = file-&gt;private_data;

	nanosic-&gt;auth_open = false;
	return 0;
}

static ssize_t nanosic_auth_read(struct file *file, char __user *buf,
				 size_t count, loff_t *off)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = file-&gt;private_data;
	struct nanosic_auth_req req;
	int ret;

	if (count != sizeof(req))
		return -EINVAL;

	ret = wait_event_interruptible(nanosic-&gt;auth_read_wq,
				       nanosic-&gt;auth_request_pending);
	if (ret)
		return ret;

	memcpy(req.uid, nanosic-&gt;auth_uid, sizeof(req.uid));
	memcpy(req.challenge, nanosic-&gt;auth_challenge, sizeof(req.challenge));
	nanosic-&gt;auth_request_pending = false;

	if (copy_to_user(buf, &amp;req, sizeof(req)))
		return -EFAULT;

	return sizeof(req);
}

static ssize_t nanosic_auth_write(struct file *file, const char __user *buf,
				  size_t count, loff_t *off)
{
	struct nanosic_wn8030 *nanosic = file-&gt;private_data;
	u8 token[16];

	if (count != sizeof(token))
		return -EINVAL;

	if (copy_from_user(token, buf, sizeof(token)))
		return -EFAULT;

	memcpy(nanosic-&gt;auth_token, token, sizeof(token));
	complete(&amp;nanosic-&gt;auth_token_ready);

	return sizeof(token);
}

static const struct file_operations nanosic_auth_fops = {
	.owner = THIS_MODULE,
	.open = nanosic_auth_open,
	.release = nanosic_auth_release,
	.read = nanosic_auth_read,
	.write = nanosic_auth_write,
};

<details><summary>🛠 bash — Read auth daemon implementation</summary>

**Input**
<pre>{
  &quot;command&quot;: &quot;cd /home/saksham/work/kernel &amp;&amp; cat configs/nanosic/nanosic-authd.py; echo \&quot;===SERVICE===\&quot;; cat configs/nanosic/nanosic-authd.service&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Read auth daemon implementation&quot;
}</pre>

**Output**
<pre>#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;Answer Nanosic WN8030 offline-auth requests from /dev/nanosic_auth.

The kernel driver forwards the MCU step-3 challenge as a 32-byte request
(uid[16] + challenge[16]) and blocks up to 5 s for a 16-byte step-5 token.
This daemon supplies that token. Token sources, in order:

  1. NANOSIC_TOKEN_FILE /etc/nanosic/auth-token (32 hex chars)
  2. tokenhelper (Android vendor HAL) if NANOSIC_TOKEN_HELPER exists
  3. a zero token in offline mode (driver key-meta 00000002)

Without any daemon the driver times out and input still flows.
&quot;&quot;&quot;

import binascii
import os
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time

DEV = os.environ.get(&quot;NANOSIC_AUTH_DEV&quot;, &quot;/dev/nanosic_auth&quot;)
TOKEN_FILE = os.environ.get(&quot;NANOSIC_TOKEN_FILE&quot;, &quot;/etc/nanosic/auth-token&quot;)
HELPER = os.environ.get(&quot;NANOSIC_TOKEN_HELPER&quot;, &quot;/usr/libexec/nanosic/tokenhelper&quot;)
KEYMETA = os.environ.get(&quot;NANOSIC_KEYMETA&quot;, &quot;00000002&quot;)
ZERO_TOKEN = bytes(16)
running = True


def log(msg):
    print(f&quot;nanosic-authd: {msg}&quot;, flush=True)


def token_from_file():
    try:
        raw = open(TOKEN_FILE, &quot;r&quot;, encoding=&quot;ascii&quot;).read().strip()
        tok = binascii.unhexlify(raw)
        return tok if len(tok) == 16 else None
    except OSError:
        return None


def token_from_helper(uid, challenge):
    if not os.access(HELPER, os.X_OK):
        return None
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            [HELPER, &quot;token&quot;, &quot;1&quot;, uid.hex(), KEYMETA, challenge.hex()],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10, check=False)
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
        log(f&quot;tokenhelper failed: {exc}&quot;)
        return None
    if out.returncode != 0:
        log(f&quot;tokenhelper rc={out.returncode}: {out.stderr.strip()}&quot;)
        return None
    try:
        tok = binascii.unhexlify(out.stdout.strip())
    except (ValueError, binascii.Error):
        return None
    return tok if len(tok) == 16 else None


def token_for(uid, challenge):
    tok = token_from_file()
    if tok:
        return tok
    tok = token_from_helper(uid, challenge)
    if tok:
        return tok
    return ZERO_TOKEN


def stop(_signum, _frame):
    global running
    running = False


def serve(fd):
    while running:
        try:
            req = os.read(fd, 32)
        except OSError as exc:
            log(f&quot;read: {exc}&quot;)
            return
        if len(req) != 32:
            return
        uid, challenge = req[:16], req[16:]
        tok = token_for(uid, challenge)
        try:
            os.write(fd, tok)
        except OSError as exc:
            log(f&quot;write: {exc}&quot;)
            return
        log(f&quot;token sent uid={uid.hex()} challenge={challenge.hex()} token={tok.hex()}&quot;)


def main():
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop)
    if token_from_file():
        log(f&quot;static token from {TOKEN_FILE}&quot;)
    elif os.access(HELPER, os.X_OK):
        log(f&quot;tokenhelper backend {HELPER} keymeta={KEYMETA}&quot;)
    else:
        log(&quot;no tokenhelper/static token: using offline zero token&quot;)
    while running:
        try:
            fd = os.open(DEV, os.O_RDWR)
        except OSError:
            time.sleep(2)
            continue
        log(f&quot;opened {DEV}&quot;)
        try:
            serve(fd)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)
            log(&quot;closed device&quot;)
        time.sleep(1)
    return 0


if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;:
    sys.exit(main())
===SERVICE===
[Unit]
Description=Nanosic WN8030 MiAuth token daemon
After=systemd-udev-settle.service
StartLimitIntervalSec=0

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/nanosic-authd
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/nanosic/authd.env
Restart=always
RestartSec=2

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
</pre>
</details>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Compile supplier-specific overlays into one early-entry selection table.
set -Eeuo pipefail
[[ $# -ge 4 &amp;&amp; -d $1 &amp;&amp; -d $2 &amp;&amp; -f $3 &amp;&amp; $4 =~ ^(36|42|auto)$ ]] || exit 2
kernel=$(realpath &quot;$1&quot;) output=$(realpath &quot;$2&quot;) source=$(realpath &quot;$3&quot;) selection=$4
shift 4
variants=(&quot;$selection&quot;)
[[ $selection != auto ]] || variants=(36 42)
header=$output/uke-native-display.h
: &gt; &quot;$header&quot;
for variant in &quot;${variants[@]}&quot;; do
    cpp -nostdinc -undef -D__DTS__ -DO82_PANEL_VARIANT=&quot;$variant&quot; -x assembler-with-cpp \
        &quot;$@&quot; -I &quot;$kernel/include&quot; &quot;$source&quot; &gt; &quot;$output/display-$variant.dts&quot;
    if [[ -n ${UKE_NATIVE_VIDEO_SOURCE:-} ]]; then
        cpp -nostdinc -undef -D__DTS__ -x assembler-with-cpp -I &quot;$kernel/include&quot; \
            &quot;$UKE_NATIVE_VIDEO_SOURCE&quot; &gt; &quot;$output/video.dts&quot;
        sed &#x27;/^\/dts-v1\/;/d; /^\/plugin\/;/d&#x27; &quot;$output/video.dts&quot; &gt;&gt; &quot;$output/display-$variant.dts&quot;
    fi
    dtc -q -@ -I dts -O dtb -o &quot;$output/display-$variant.dtbo&quot; &quot;$output/display-$variant.dts&quot;
    {
        printf &#x27;static unsigned char uke_native_overlay_%s[] __initdata __aligned(8) = {\n&#x27; &quot;$variant&quot;
        od -An -v -tx1 &quot;$output/display-$variant.dtbo&quot; | sed -E &#x27;s/[a-f0-9]{2}/0x&amp;,/g&#x27;
        printf &#x27;};\n&#x27;
    } &gt;&gt; &quot;$header&quot;
done
{
    printf &#x27;static const struct uke_native_panel uke_native_panels[] __initconst = {\n&#x27;
    for variant in &quot;${variants[@]}&quot;; do
        if [[ $variant == 36 ]]; then suffix=36_02_0a; else suffix=42_02_0b; fi
        printf &#x27;\t{ &quot;msm_drm.dsi_display0=qcom,mdss_dsi_o82_%s_dualdsi_dsc_vid&quot;, uke_native_overlay_%s, sizeof(uke_native_overlay_%s) },\n&#x27; &quot;$suffix&quot; &quot;$variant&quot; &quot;$variant&quot;
    done
    printf &#x27;};\n&#x27;
} &gt;&gt; &quot;$header&quot;
# Retain the historical fixture filenames; boot uses the complete table above.
cp &quot;$output/display-${variants[-1]}.dts&quot; &quot;$output/display.dts&quot;
cp &quot;$output/display-${variants[-1]}.dtbo&quot; &quot;$output/display.dtbo&quot;
install -m644 &quot;$header&quot; &quot;$kernel/arch/arm64/kernel/uke-native-display.h&quot;

on:

    branches: [main, fix/focus-keyboard]

        type: string

    timeout-minutes: 300
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository and submodules
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Ensure submodule legacy refs
        run: |
          git -C uke-linux-hardware-support fetch origin legacy-1.5.2:refs/tags/legacy-1.5.2 || true

      - name: Record component pins
        id: pins

      - name: Free disk space
        run: |

          sudo docker system prune -af --volumes 2&gt;/dev/null || true
          sudo apt-get clean
          df -h /

      - name: Install host tools
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends jq zstd g++ python3 python3-cryptography python3-pip e2fsprogs curl ca-certificates

            | base64 -d | sudo tee /usr/local/bin/avbtool &gt;/dev/null

          avbtool --help &gt;/dev/null

            build/release-*/SHA256SUMS
          if-no-files-found: warn
          compression-level: 0

<pre>#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;Apply the CI-only overlay to the pinned submodule trees.

The submodules point at upstream repositories this fork cannot push to, so the
build workflow applies this overlay on the runner before building. Every
replacement is asserted: a silent no-op means a broken image, not a skipped
feature.
&quot;&quot;&quot;
import argparse
import pathlib

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def replace_once(rel, old, new, writes):
    path = ROOT / rel
    text = path.read_text()
    count = text.count(old)
    if count != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f&quot;{rel}: expected exactly one match, found {count}: {old[:70]!r}&quot;)
    if writes:
        path.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1))


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument(&quot;--check&quot;, action=&quot;store_true&quot;, help=&quot;validate patterns without writing&quot;)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    writes = not args.check

    builder = &quot;uke-fedora-builder&quot;
    kernel = &quot;senemos-uke-kernel&quot;
    hardware = &quot;uke-linux-hardware-support&quot;

    # OEM firmware count grows with the uke-oem-data RPM.
    replace_once(f&quot;{builder}/src/image/verify-oem-rpm.sh&quot;,
                 &quot;[[ $count == 74 ]]&quot;, &quot;[[ $count == 75 ]]&quot;, writes)
    replace_once(f&quot;{builder}/src/image/audit-rootfs.sh&quot;,
                 &quot;((firmware_count == 74))&quot;, &quot;((firmware_count == 75))&quot;, writes)

    # The workflow runs the builder with Docker on the runner.
    replace_once(f&quot;{builder}/build-rootfs.sh&quot;,
                 &quot;if command -v podman &gt;/dev/null; then container=podman&quot;,
                 &quot;if [[ -n ${UKE_CONTAINER:-} ]]; then container=$UKE_CONTAINER; &quot;
                 &quot;elif command -v podman &gt;/dev/null; then container=podman&quot;, writes)

    # Pull the OEM data RPM into the primary transaction.
    replace_once(f&quot;{builder}/build-rootfs.sh&quot;,
                 &quot;        /core-rpm/uke-core-meta.rpm\n&quot;,
                 &quot;        /core-rpm/uke-core-meta.rpm /hardware-rpms/uke-fedora*-oem-data-*.rpm\n&quot;,
                 writes)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;Fallback overlay: 6 GiB zram and the native Iris video path.

Applied only when the base build fails. Every replacement is asserted.
&quot;&quot;&quot;
import argparse
import pathlib

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def replace_once(rel, old, new, writes):
    path = ROOT / rel
    text = path.read_text()
    count = text.count(old)
    if count != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f&quot;{rel}: expected one match, found {count}: {old[:70]!r}&quot;)
    if writes:
        path.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1))


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument(&quot;--check&quot;, action=&quot;store_true&quot;)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    writes = not args.check

    # 6 GiB zram: enough for KDE + browser on 8 GiB while keeping headroom.
    replace_once(&quot;uke-fedora-builder/configs/images/uke-zram-generator.conf&quot;,
                 &quot;zram-size = min(ram / 2, 4096)&quot;, &quot;zram-size = min(ram * 3 / 4, 6144)&quot;, writes)
    replace_once(&quot;uke-fedora-builder/src/image/audit-rootfs.sh&quot;,
                 &quot;grep -Fxq &#x27;zram-size = min(ram / 2, 4096)&#x27;&quot;,
                 &quot;grep -Fxq &#x27;zram-size = min(ram * 3 / 4, 6144)&#x27;&quot;, writes)

    # Native Iris video: instantiate the DT node and install its VPU firmware.
    replace_once(
        &quot;uke-fedora-builder/build-rootfs.sh&quot;,
        &quot;if [[ $copr == 1 ]]; then\n&quot;,
        &#x27;sudo install -Dm644 &quot;$here/../uke-linux-hardware-support/xiaomi-uke-firmware/payload/oem-os3.0.304.0/firmware/qcom/vpu/vpu30_2v.mbn&quot; &#x27;
        &#x27;&quot;$output/root/usr/lib/firmware/qcom/uke/vpu30_2v.mbn&quot;\n&#x27;
        &quot;if [[ $copr == 1 ]]; then\n&quot;,
        writes)

    # The VA-API stage is an extra build stage beyond the stock count.
    replace_once(
        &quot;uke-fedora-builder/build-images.sh&quot;,
        &quot;build_total=$((12 + 2 * ${#build_profiles[@]}))&quot;,
        &quot;build_total=$((13 + 2 * ${#build_profiles[@]}))&quot;,
        writes)

    # Build and install the stateful Iris VA-API backend so browsers actually
    # pick the hardware decoder instead of software decoding.
    replace_once(
        &quot;uke-fedora-builder/build-images.sh&quot;,
        &quot;make -C uke-linux-hardware-support/xiaomi-uke-firmware image-data-srpm\n&quot;,
        &quot;make -C uke-linux-hardware-support/xiaomi-uke-firmware image-data-srpm\n&quot;
        &quot;make -C uke-linux-hardware-support/uke-video srpm\n&quot;,
        writes)
    replace_once(
        &quot;uke-fedora-builder/build-images.sh&quot;,
        &quot;  uke-linux-hardware-support/uke-boot/build/srpm/rpmbuild\n&quot;,
        &quot;  uke-linux-hardware-support/uke-boot/build/srpm/rpmbuild\n&quot;
        &quot;  uke-linux-hardware-support/uke-video/build/srpm\n&quot;,
        writes)
    replace_once(
        &quot;uke-fedora-builder/build-images.sh&quot;,
        &quot;        */uke-boot/*) component=boot-integration;;\n&quot;,
        &quot;        */uke-boot/*) component=boot-integration;;\n&quot;
        &quot;        */uke-video/*) component=vaapi;;\n&quot;,
        writes)
    replace_once(
        &quot;uke-fedora-builder/build-images.sh&quot;,
        &#x27;cp &quot;$workspace&quot;/uke-linux-hardware-support/xiaomi-uke-firmware/build/fedora${release}-image-data/rpmbuild/RPMS/noarch/uke-fedora${release}-oem-data-3.0.304.0-2.fc${release}.noarch.rpm &quot;$hardware_rpms/&quot;\n&#x27;,

        &#x27;cp &quot;$workspace&quot;/uke-linux-hardware-support/uke-video/build/srpm/RPMS/aarch64/uke-vaapi-v4l2-1.0.0-*.fc${release}.aarch64.rpm &quot;$hardware_rpms/&quot;\n&#x27;,
        writes)
    replace_once(
        &quot;uke-fedora-builder/build-rootfs.sh&quot;,

<pre>{
  &quot;content&quot;: &quot;#!/bin/bash\n# Hot-load the Xiaomi Focus Keyboard (Nanosic WN8030) on a running kernel.\n# Run as root:  sudo /home/saksham/focus-keyboard/install.sh\nset -Eeuo pipefail\n\nhere=$(cd -- \&quot;$(dirname -- \&quot;$0\&quot;)\&quot; &amp;&amp; pwd)\nkver=$(uname -r)\nfw=/usr/lib/firmware/nanosic/MCU_Upgrade.bin\nmoddir=/lib/modules/$kver/extra\novl=/sys/kernel/config/device-tree/overlays/focus-keyboard\n\n[ \&quot;$(id -u)\&quot; = 0 ] || { echo \&quot;run as root\&quot; &gt;&amp;2; exit 1; }\n[ -e /sys/kernel/config/device-tree/overlays ] || {\n    echo \&quot;device-tree overlay configfs is unavailable\&quot; &gt;&amp;2; exit 1;\n}\n\necho \&quot;== firmware ==\&quot;\ninstall -Dm644 \&quot;$here/MCU_Upgrade.bin\&quot; \&quot;$fw\&quot;\nls -l \&quot;$fw\&quot;\n\necho \&quot;== module ==\&quot;\ninstall -Dm644 \&quot;$here/hid-nanosic-wn8030.ko\&quot; \&quot;$moddir/hid-nanosic-wn8030.ko\&quot;\ndepmod -a \&quot;$kver\&quot;\nmodinfo -F vermagic \&quot;$moddir/hid-nanosic-wn8030.ko\&quot;\n\necho \&quot;== device-tree overlay ==\&quot;\nif [ -e \&quot;$ovl/status\&quot; ]; then\n    echo \&quot;overlay already applied: $(cat \&quot;$ovl/status\&quot;)\&quot;\nelse\n    mkdir -p \&quot;$ovl\&quot;\n    cat \&quot;$here/focus-keyboard.dtbo\&quot; &gt; \&quot;$ovl/dtbo\&quot;\n    sleep 1\n    echo \&quot;overlay status: $(cat \&quot;$ovl/status\&quot; 2&gt;/dev/null || echo unknown)\&quot;\nfi\n\necho \&quot;== i2c controller ==\&quot;\nfor d in /sys/bus/platform/devices/*.i2c; do\n    [ -e \&quot;$d\&quot; ] || continue\n    name=$(basename \&quot;$d\&quot;)\n    case \&quot;$name\&quot; in\n    a8c000.i2c)\n        if [ ! -e \&quot;$d/driver\&quot; ]; then\n            echo \&quot;$name\&quot; &gt; /sys/bus/platform/drivers/geni_i2c/bind 2&gt;/dev/null || true\n        fi\n        echo \&quot;$name -&gt; $(readlink \&quot;$d/driver\&quot; 2&gt;/dev/null || echo unbound)\&quot;\n        ;;\n    esac\ndone\nfor b in /sys/bus/i2c/devices/i2c-*; do\n    [ -e \&quot;$b/name\&quot; ] || continue\n    case \&quot;$(cat \&quot;$b/name\&quot;)\&quot; in\n    *a8c000*) echo \&quot;bus $(basename \&quot;$b\&quot;) = $(cat \&quot;$b/name\&quot;)\&quot;;;\n    esac\ndone\n\necho \&quot;== driver ==\&quot;\nmodprobe hid-nanosic-wn8030 2&gt;/dev/null || insmod \&quot;$moddir/hid-nanosic-wn8030.ko\&quot;\nlsmod | grep -E &#x27;hid_nanosic|hid_multitouch&#x27; || true\n\necho \&quot;== optional auth daemon (not started) ==\&quot;\ninstall -Dm755 \&quot;$here/nanosic-authd.py\&quot; /usr/local/sbin/nanosic-authd\ninstall -Dm644 \&quot;$here/nanosic-authd.service\&quot; /usr/lib/systemd/system/nanosic-authd.service\nsystemctl daemon-reload\necho \&quot;start it with: systemctl enable --now nanosic-authd\&quot;\n\necho \&quot;== result ==\&quot;\nsleep 1\ndmesg | tail -40\necho \&quot;--- input devices ---\&quot;\ngrep -iE &#x27;nanosic|xiaomi|keyboard|touchpad&#x27; /proc/bus/input/devices || true\necho \&quot;--- leds ---\&quot;\nls -l /sys/class/leds/nanosic* 2&gt;/dev/null || true\necho \&quot;--- auth node ---\&quot;\nls -l /dev/nanosic_auth 2&gt;/dev/null || true\n&quot;,

<details><summary>🛠 write — home/saksham/focus-keyboard/README.md</summary>

**Input**
<pre>{
  &quot;content&quot;: &quot;# Xiaomi Focus Keyboard (Nanosic WN8030) hot-load kit\n\nBuilt for the running kernel **7.3.1-106** on the Xiaomi Pad 7 (uke).\n\nThe kernel module was built from the staged driver in\n`saksham-991/senemos-uke-kernel-mainline` (`2e2a114`), matching the running\nkernel&#x27;s config and vermagic.  The overlay normalizes the OEM `qupv3_se3`\ncontroller (`i2c@a8c000`) to the mainline `qcom,geni-i2c` binding, enables\nit, and merges the standard WN8030 properties into the existing\n`nanosic@4c` node.\n\nRun:\n\n```sh\nsudo /home/saksham/focus-keyboard/install.sh\n```\n\nExpected after a successful probe:\n\n```\nhid-nanosic-wn8030  ...  Nanosic WN8030 keyboard MCU\ninput: Xiaomi Focus Keyboard as /devices/.../input/inputNN\ninput: Xiaomi Focus Keyboard Touchpad as /devices/.../input/inputNN\n/sys/class/leds/nanosic::kbd_backlight\n/sys/class/leds/nanosic::micmute\n```\n\nThe auth daemon is optional.  The driver sends the MiAuth start and step-3\nframes and chooses the key-meta candidate advertised by the MCU.  Without a\ntoken provider it deliberately skips step 5 instead of stalling the IRQ\nthread.  To try the zero-token offline path:\n\n```sh\nsudo systemctl enable --now nanosic-authd\n```\n\nA real MiAuth token still needs the Xiaomi `devauth` trustlet (the Android\n`midevauthd`/`tokenhelper` path).  `/dev/tee0` exists on this kernel; that\nport is the remaining TrustZone work.\n&quot;,

}</pre>

**Output**
<pre># Xiaomi Pad 7 / 7 Pro Keyboard Fix

Hardware keyboard fixes for the **Xiaomi Pad 7 (`uke`)** and **Pad 7 Pro (`muyu`)** running custom AOSP or crDroid ROMs.

Restores typing at boot, fixes landscape arrow key rotation, enables the Caps Lock LED, adds keyboard backlight shortcuts, and resolves excessive CPU usage caused by Xiaomi&#x27;s touch telemetry service.

## Quick Install — Magisk / KernelSU

1. Download **Xiaomi-Pad7-Keyboard-Fix-All-in-One.zip** from the [latest release](https://github.com/saksham-991/xiaomi-keyboard-fix/releases/tag/Magisk-Module).
2. Install the ZIP through Magisk or KernelSU.
3. Reboot your tablet.

&gt;Magisk Module is **not needed** to install, it is just for convenience, manual steps to write out all the commands are given below which essentially do the exact same thing that this module does.

## Problems Solved

| Problem | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Keyboard connects but cannot type | `xiaomi_kbd_service.sh` automates HID rebinding at boot and when the keyboard connects. |
| Keyboard stops working after a few minutes | `kbd_auth.sh` and `tokenhelper` provide MiAuth tokens locally through TrustZone. |
| Arrow keys are rotated 90° in landscape | `kbd_idc.sh` generates the IDC configuration early in boot with `device.internal = 0`. |
| Caps Lock LED does not work | `kbd_leds.sh` watches input events and synchronizes the LED state. |
| Keyboard backlight cannot be adjusted | `kbd_leds.sh` adds configurable brightness shortcuts. |
| Tablet overheats or one CPU core stays at 100% | `kbd_no_toucheventcheck.sh` disables the broken MiSight touch telemetry loop. |

&gt; The 30hz touchpad issue (choppy pointer) is also solved in the magisk module as it is a simple toggle &quot;Disable HW Overlays&quot; IN developer options, I added it here because the touchpad is on the same keyboard folio case, otherwise its basically a ROM issue, rather than a Keyboard issue.

### Security and Privacy

No keystrokes are logged. Authentication keys are not extracted or sent online. Authentication tokens are computed locally using the stock firmware&#x27;s `devauth` trustlets.

## Manual Installation

Use this method to install the fix through `/data/adb` boot scripts without installing a Magisk module.

### Prerequisites

- A Xiaomi Pad 7 or Pad 7 Pro running a custom ROM with stock HyperOS vendor blobs.
- Root access through Magisk or KernelSU.
- ADB Setup.
- The following three proprietary HAL files extracted from the `odm.img` partition of a stock HyperOS Recovery ROM&#x27;s payload.bin using EROFS:

  ```text
  /odm/bin/midevauthd
  /odm/lib64/libmidevauth.so
  /odm/lib64/vendor.xiaomi.hardware.aidl.midevauth-V1-ndk_platform.so
  ```

- The `tokenhelper` binary from the [latest release](https://github.com/JohnnyFFM/xiaomi-keyboard-fix/releases/latest), or a manually built copy.
- The scripts from this repository&#x27;s `device/` directory.

Check that the required firmware and device interface are present:

```sh
adb shell su -c &#x27;ls /vendor/firmware_mnt/image/devauth.*; ls /dev/smcinvoke&#x27;
```

### 1. Stage the Files

Run this command on your computer from the repository directory, with the extracted HAL files and `tokenhelper` in the current directory:

```sh
adb push \
  midevauthd \
  libmidevauth.so \
  vendor.xiaomi.hardware.aidl.midevauth-V1-ndk_platform.so \
  tokenhelper \
  device/kbd_auth.sh \
  device/kbd_leds.sh \
  device/service.d-kbdauth.sh \
  device/xiaomi_kbd_service.sh \
  device/post-fs-data-kbd-idc.sh \
  device/kbd_no_toucheventcheck.sh \
  /data/local/tmp/
```

### 2. Install the Files and Set Permissions

```sh
adb shell su -c &#x27;
mkdir -p /data/adb/kbdauth /data/adb/service.d /data/adb/post-fs-data.d

cp \
  /data/local/tmp/midevauthd \
  /data/local/tmp/libmidevauth.so \
  /data/local/tmp/vendor.xiaomi.hardware.aidl.midevauth-V1-ndk_platform.so \
  /data/local/tmp/tokenhelper \
  /data/local/tmp/kbd_auth.sh \
  /data/local/tmp/kbd_leds.sh \
  /data/adb/kbdauth/

cp /data/local/tmp/service.d-kbdauth.sh \
  /data/adb/service.d/kbdauth.sh

cp /data/local/tmp/xiaomi_kbd_service.sh \
  /data/adb/service.d/xiaomi_kbd_service.sh

cp /data/local/tmp/post-fs-data-kbd-idc.sh \
  /data/adb/post-fs-data.d/kbd_idc.sh

cp /data/local/tmp/kbd_no_toucheventcheck.sh \
  /data/adb/post-fs-data.d/kbd_no_toucheventcheck.sh

chmod 755 \
  /data/adb/kbdauth/midevauthd \
  /data/adb/kbdauth/tokenhelper \
  /data/adb/kbdauth/kbd_auth.sh \
  /data/adb/kbdauth/kbd_leds.sh \
  /data/adb/service.d/kbdauth.sh \
  /data/adb/service.d/xiaomi_kbd_service.sh \
  /data/adb/post-fs-data.d/kbd_idc.sh \
  /data/adb/post-fs-data.d/kbd_no_toucheventcheck.sh
&#x27;
```

### 3. Reboot

```sh
adb reboot
```

Thanks for the report — that &quot;works for a few minutes then stops&quot; is exactly the dropout the old module couldn&#x27;t fix, and I think I finally have the real cause.

I&#x27;ve pushed a new approach (**v2.0.0**, now on `master`; the old module is preserved on the `legacy-hid-rebind` branch): instead of rebinding the HID, it **completes the keyboard&#x27;s MiAuth handshake by computing the real authentication token with the tablet&#x27;s own TrustZone key** (via the stock `midevauthd` HAL + a tiny binder client), which is what stock HyperOS does and custom ROMs don&#x27;t.

One caveat: it&#x27;s tested on the Pad 7 **Pro** (`muyu`), and you&#x27;re on the Pad 7 (`uke`), so I can&#x27;t be sure the same secure components are present. Could you check these exist first:

## v3 is out — now an all-in-one fix 🎉

Thanks again @saksham-991 for confirming v2 worked on `uke`. **v3.0.0** bundles everything into one install (no more manual `bind`/`unbind`):

1. **HID enable** (`xiaomi_kbd_service.sh`) — on a custom ROM the keyboard&#x27;s HID is registered at boot but left *disabled*, so keystrokes are dropped. This rebinds it while connected, which re-enables it. (This is the manual bind step you had to do — now automatic.)
2. **Auth keep-alive** (`kbd_auth.sh` + stock `midevauthd`) — completes Xiaomi&#x27;s MiAuth using the tablet&#x27;s own TrustZone key, so the keyboard doesn&#x27;t stop after a while.
3. **Caps Lock LED** (`kbd_leds.sh`) — tracks Caps Lock in real time.
4. **Keyboard backlight** (`kbd_leds.sh`) — the keyboard&#x27;s own **Fn backlight keys** (illum up / down / toggle) adjust it, 0–100, like stock.

Grab the prebuilt `tokenhelper` from the **[v3.0.0 release](https://github.com/JohnnyFFM/xiaomi-keyboard-fix/releases/tag/v3.0.0)** and follow the updated README. (v2 is preserved on the `v2-backup` branch.)

&gt; Note: the `tokenhelper` binary is **bit-identical** to v2.0.0 (same source), so if you already have it you don&#x27;t need to rebuild/re-download — only the shell scripts changed.

### 🙏 Need a backlight confirmation
My test tablet&#x27;s keyboard is **not backlit**, so I could only verify the backlight *pipeline* (the Fn backlight keys are detected and the command is sent) — I can&#x27;t see the light. **If you have a backlit keyboard, could you install v3 and confirm that the Fn backlight keys actually change the backlight?** If it&#x27;s off or the steps feel wrong, the knobs `BL_STEP` / `BL_DEFAULT` / `BL_MAX` at the top of `device/kbd_leds.sh` can be tuned — let me know what you see in `/data/adb/kbd/leds.log` (look for `backlight=NN` lines) and I&#x27;ll adjust.

Caps Lock + no-dropout + auto-enable are all confirmed working; backlight is the one piece needing a backlit unit to sign off. Thanks!

Thanks for testing v3 — great that Caps Lock is solid! And thanks for the backlight details; that explains it: the Focus Keyboard has no backlight keys, and HyperOS drove it from the Settings slider / auto (light sensor), neither of which exists on crDroid.

So we need to pick how to control it here. **Which would you prefer?** (We can also combine.)

1. **A small app** — a tiny APK with an on/off toggle + brightness slider for the keyboard backlight. Doable: the app just writes the chosen level and a root helper sends it to the keyboard.
2. **Key combos** — remap a few keys, e.g. **Fn+3 / Fn+4 / Fn+5 = off / dimmer / brighter**, so you can adjust it from the keyboard itself.
3. **Mirror the display brightness** — the keyboard backlight follows the tablet&#x27;s screen brightness. Since screen auto-brightness already tracks ambient light, this basically gives you the HyperOS &quot;auto-backlit&quot; behaviour for free, with no extra moving parts.

I&#x27;d lean away from tapping the ambient light sensor directly: that needs a separate always-running process going through Android&#x27;s sensor framework (not reachable from the lightweight root scripts this uses), and option 3 already gives you the ambient behaviour via the screen-brightness proxy. A nice combo could be **the slider app + display-brightness auto as the default**.

Let me know your preference and I&#x27;ll build it.

On your other two points — the **arrow keys rotated 90°** and defaulting **&quot;Disable HW overlays&quot;** for the 30 Hz touchpad feel — thanks, I&#x27;ll look into those. They&#x27;re separate from the keyboard-firmware fix (a keylayout remap and a display/dev setting respectively), so I&#x27;ll track them on their own rather than in this keyboard module.

<details><summary>🛠 bash — Read tokenhelper source</summary>

**Input**
<pre>{
  &quot;command&quot;: &quot;cd /home/saksham/work/keyboardfix &amp;&amp; sed -n &#x27;1,160p&#x27; src/tokenhelper.cpp&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Read tokenhelper source&quot;
}</pre>

**Output**
<pre>// tokenhelper — tiny bridge between the keyboard handshake (shell) and the
// MiDevAuth TrustZone HAL (midevauthd) on the Xiaomi Pad 7 Pro (muyu).
//
// It performs ONE binder call: IMidevauthService.devauth_token_get(type, uid,
// keyMeta, challenge) and prints the resulting token as hex. The keyboard
// re-auth handshake itself is driven by the shell script that calls this.
//
// Usage:
//   tokenhelper token  &lt;type&gt; &lt;uid_hex&gt; &lt;keyMeta_hex&gt; &lt;challenge_hex&gt;
//   tokenhelper verify &lt;type&gt; &lt;uid_hex&gt; &lt;keyMeta_hex&gt; &lt;challenge_hex&gt; &lt;kbdToken_hex&gt;
//   tokenhelper keyver
//   tokenhelper offlinecheck &lt;keyMeta_hex&gt;
// Prints the result (token as hex, or an int) to stdout; errors to stderr.

#include &lt;aidl/vendor/xiaomi/hardware/aidl/midevauth/IMidevauthService.h&gt;
#include &lt;android/binder_auto_utils.h&gt;
#include &lt;dlfcn.h&gt;
// AServiceManager_* lives in android/binder_manager.h, which is a system/LLNDK
// header absent from the public NDK. Resolve it at runtime from the device&#x27;s
// libbinder_ndk.so via dlsym so we only link against NDK-public symbols.

#include &lt;cstdio&gt;
#include &lt;cstdlib&gt;
#include &lt;cstring&gt;
#include &lt;string&gt;
#include &lt;vector&gt;

using aidl::vendor::xiaomi::hardware::aidl::midevauth::IMidevauthService;

static int nib(char c) {
    if (c &gt;= &#x27;0&#x27; &amp;&amp; c &lt;= &#x27;9&#x27;) return c - &#x27;0&#x27;;
    c = (char)(c | 0x20);
    if (c &gt;= &#x27;a&#x27; &amp;&amp; c &lt;= &#x27;f&#x27;) return c - &#x27;a&#x27; + 10;
    return -1;
}

static bool parse_hex(const char* s, std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt;&amp; out) {
    out.clear();
    for (size_t i = 0; s[i]; ) {
        if (s[i] == &#x27; &#x27; || s[i] == &#x27;:&#x27;) { i++; continue; }      // allow &quot;aa bb&quot; / &quot;aa:bb&quot;
        int hi = nib(s[i]);
        int lo = s[i + 1] ? nib(s[i + 1]) : -1;
        if (hi &lt; 0 || lo &lt; 0) return false;
        out.push_back((uint8_t)((hi &lt;&lt; 4) | lo));
        i += 2;
    }
    return true;
}

static void print_hex(const std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt;&amp; v) {
    for (uint8_t b : v) printf(&quot;%02x&quot;, b);
    printf(&quot;\n&quot;);
}

static std::shared_ptr&lt;IMidevauthService&gt; get_service() {
    const char* name = &quot;vendor.xiaomi.hardware.aidl.midevauth.IMidevauthService/default&quot;;
    void* h = dlopen(&quot;libbinder_ndk.so&quot;, RTLD_NOW);
    if (!h) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;tokenhelper: dlopen libbinder_ndk.so: %s\n&quot;, dlerror()); return nullptr; }
    using fn_t = AIBinder* (*)(const char*);
    AIBinder* raw = nullptr;
    if (auto w = (fn_t)dlsym(h, &quot;AServiceManager_waitForService&quot;)) raw = w(name);
    else if (auto g = (fn_t)dlsym(h, &quot;AServiceManager_getService&quot;)) raw = g(name);
    else { fprintf(stderr, &quot;tokenhelper: no AServiceManager_* symbol\n&quot;); return nullptr; }
    if (!raw) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;tokenhelper: service &#x27;%s&#x27; not found\n&quot;, name); return nullptr; }
    ndk::SpAIBinder bin(raw);
    auto svc = IMidevauthService::fromBinder(bin);
    if (!svc) fprintf(stderr, &quot;tokenhelper: fromBinder returned null\n&quot;);
    return svc;
}

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    if (argc &lt; 2) {
        fprintf(stderr, &quot;usage: tokenhelper &lt;token|verify|keyver|offlinecheck&gt; ...\n&quot;);
        return 2;
    }
    const std::string cmd = argv[1];
    auto svc = get_service();
    if (!svc) return 3;

    if (cmd == &quot;keyver&quot;) {
        int32_t v = -1;
        auto st = svc-&gt;devauth_key_version(&amp;v);
        if (!st.isOk()) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;key_version: %s\n&quot;, st.getDescription().c_str()); return 4; }
        printf(&quot;%d\n&quot;, v);
        return 0;
    }

    if (cmd == &quot;offlinecheck&quot;) {
        if (argc &lt; 3) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;offlinecheck &lt;keyMeta_hex&gt;\n&quot;); return 2; }
        std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt; km;
        if (!parse_hex(argv[2], km)) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;bad hex\n&quot;); return 2; }
        int32_t r = -1;
        auto st = svc-&gt;devauth_OfflineMasterKey_check(km, &amp;r);
        if (!st.isOk()) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;offline_check: %s\n&quot;, st.getDescription().c_str()); return 4; }
        printf(&quot;%d\n&quot;, r);   // 0 == valid (per stock chooseKey)
        return 0;
    }

    if (cmd == &quot;token&quot; || cmd == &quot;verify&quot;) {
        int need = (cmd == &quot;token&quot;) ? 6 : 7;
        if (argc &lt; need) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;not enough args for %s\n&quot;, cmd.c_str()); return 2; }
        int type = atoi(argv[2]);
        std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt; uid, km, ch;
        if (!parse_hex(argv[3], uid) || !parse_hex(argv[4], km) || !parse_hex(argv[5], ch)) {
            fprintf(stderr, &quot;bad hex in uid/keyMeta/challenge\n&quot;); return 2;
        }
        if (cmd == &quot;token&quot;) {
            std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt; out;
            auto st = svc-&gt;devauth_token_get(type, uid, km, ch, &amp;out);
            if (!st.isOk()) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;token_get: %s\n&quot;, st.getDescription().c_str()); return 4; }
            if (out.empty()) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;token_get: empty token\n&quot;); return 5; }
            print_hex(out);
            return 0;
        } else {
            std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt; tok;
            if (!parse_hex(argv[6], tok)) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;bad hex token\n&quot;); return 2; }
            int32_t r = -1;
            auto st = svc-&gt;devauth_token_verify(type, uid, km, ch, tok, &amp;r);
            if (!st.isOk()) { fprintf(stderr, &quot;token_verify: %s\n&quot;, st.getDescription().c_str()); return 4; }
            printf(&quot;%d\n&quot;, r);  // 1 online pass, 2 offline pass, else fail
            return 0;
        }
    }

    fprintf(stderr, &quot;unknown command &#x27;%s&#x27;\n&quot;, cmd.c_str());
    return 2;
}
</pre>
</details>
